title: Selma Blair arrested after in-flight incident
summary: Selma Blair, 54, was arraigned on two assault charges after she was arrested and hospitalized Sunday in New York. The actress allegedly attacked crew members mid-air on a Delta flight from Los Angeles.
story: The actress was arrested Sunday after allegedly attacking crew members on board a Delta flight into New York City. (Credit: Rashid Umar Abbasi for Fox News)

Selma Blair was arraigned Monday on two counts of second-degree assault for reportedly assaulting a nurse and a police officer after allegedly attacking crew members on board a Delta flight into New York City, the Associated Press reported.
The judge set bail at $20,000 cash/$60,000 bond/ $60,000 partially secured bond. She's expected in court in January 2027.
The actress was arrested Sunday aboard the flight from LA to NYC.

"On Sunday October 11 at approximately 11pm at JFK Airport, PAPD responded to a call about a physically abusive passenger aboard Delta Airlines flight 938 which was parked at the gate after arrival from LAX," New York Port Authority officials confirmed to Fox News Digital.
"Suspect was identified as Selma Blair, a 54-year-old woman. She was taken into custody and transported to the hospital for evaluation."
SELMA BLAIR SAYS ‘NO ONE RETURNED MY CALLS’ AFTER ANTI-ISLAM COMMENT LED TO HOLLYWOOD FALLOUT
Selma Blair seen exiting the courthouse in Queens on Monday, Oct. 12, 2026. (Rashid Umar Abbasi for Fox News)

Blair appeared in Queens Criminal Court in Queens, New York. The actress was arrested Sunday after allegedly attacking crew members on board a Delta flight into New York City. (Barry Williams/ New York Daily News via Pool)
During her court appearance in Queens, Blair’s lawyer claimed the actress missed multiple doses of a "powerful" medication, The New York Post reported.

"This was not an intentional assault," the outlet noted that her attorney, Shawn Barnes, said in court. "Ms. Blair missed several doses of… a powerful medication that controls severe neurological symptoms."

"Ms. Blair boarded this flight after being on set and working extensive hours and exhaustive hours in the days leading up to this flight," he added. "Additionally, at one point, during the flight, there was an incident where Miss Blair actually fell and hit her head," Barnes added, according to The NY Post. "These factors, coupled with altitude, resulted in a state of severe confusion and disorientation."
During her court appearance, Blair’s lawyer claimed she missed multiple doses of a "powerful" medication, The New York Post reported. (Barry Williams/ New York Daily News via Pool)
Federal charges will be handled separately.
Blair was restrained on a stretcher at the airport but freed her leg, and allegedly kicked the officer in the face, neck and chest, causing substantial swelling, court documents said via AP.
The nurse at Jamaica Hospital Medical Center, where Blair was taken, alleged that the actress kicked her in the chest while moving her.
The actress pictured in handcuffs in court Monday. (Barry Williams/ New York Daily News via Pool)
Blair stood before a judge one day after the incident. (Barry Williams/ New York Daily News via Pool)
Blair pictured with her attorney. (Barry Williams/ New York Daily News via Pool)
Blair was arraigned Monday before a judge. (Rashid Umar Abbasi for Fox News)
Federal charges will be handled separately, AP reported. (Rashid Umar Abbasi for Fox News)
Law enforcement officials confirmed Blair was served with a summons by the FBI, and is currently facing one charge of assault.

"Selma experienced a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct. Upon landing, she received immediate medical attention and is currently in stable condition," a rep confirmed to Fox News Digital.
SELMA BLAIR SAYS SHE'S TRULY RELAPSE-FREE' AFTER 7-YEAR BATTLE WITH MS
Blair appeared to break her silence Monday in a comment on Instagram from her whirlwind travels where she wrote, "I'm. It great. I'm sad. I'm grateful. I hope. I am not great."
"From LA to New Mexico to La to nyc to LA Scout and I have been busy," she captioned a video montage. "I miss you."
Blair seen leaving the courthouse on Monday night. (Rashid Umar Abbasi for Fox News)
Officials confirmed two flight attendants also reported injuries, and one was transported to the hospital for further evaluation.

"We'd like to have some medical personnel at the gate for a couple of the FA's [flight attendants] involved in the passenger incident," dispatch requested in audio obtained by Fox News Digital. "They just need to get a couple things looked at."
Blair was charged with two counts of assault.  (Rashid Umar Abbasi for Fox News)
WATCH: SELMA BLAIR REPORTEDLY BIT FLIGHT ATTENDANT, TRIED TO OPEN PLANE DOOR DURING FLIGHT
Selma Blair was taken into custody and transported to the hospital for evaluation following an in-air incident on a Delta flight. (Gilbert Flores/Variety via Getty Images)
Delta confirmed that law enforcement officials responded to an incident upon arrival to John F. Kennedy International Airport, a flight which departed out of Los Angeles earlier in the day.

"Delta has zero tolerance for unruly or unlawful behavior, as the safety of our customers and crew always comes first," Delta said in a statement.

Additionally, there was no operational impact on the flight as it landed ahead of schedule at JFK, Delta said.
Sources told TMZ that Blair allegedly punched one flight attendant and bit another in the middle of the flight.
She was traveling with her service dog, which is now in the custody of her attorney, CBS reported.

In her 2022 memoir, "Mean Baby: A Memoir of Growing Up," Blair disclosed a history of biting celebrities.
Selma Blair was previously involved in a mid-air incident on board a Delta flight in 2016. (Dimitrios Kambouris/Getty Images for Glamour)
"My system gets overwhelmed and instantaneously short-circuits … In my life, social interactions have been cumbersome," she wrote, according to Page Six.
One particular incident allegedly involved Sienna Miller.

"I couldn‘t begrudge her for any part she was winning over me," Blair wrote. "So, I grabbed her arm and bit it, playfully, as if it were an apple. Even as I held her forearm in my mouth I was aghast at myself. I thought, What have I gotten myself into? Or her? This is horrible behavior."
In addition, Blair claimed she bit "Family Guy" creator Seth MacFarlane, who she became "starstruck" with after seeing the media mogul at a club in Las Vegas.

"What do I do in public situations where I admire someone, but feel as if I don’t bring anything to the party? I bit him on the hand. ‘Whoa!’ he yelled. ‘That really hurt.’ It wasn’t a disaster; I didn’t break skin. But I soon hated myself," Blair wrote.

TMZ reported at the time that Blair was crying and saying things like, "He burns my private parts. He won't let me eat or drink," and that she was removed from the aircraft via stretcher and taken to the hospital.

title: Ben Affleck has blunt response to teenage son's Lamborghini request after infamous mishap
summary: Ben Affleck revealed his son Samuel asked him to buy a Lamborghini, four years after the teen's infamous fender-bender at a luxury car dealership.
story: Actor Ben Affleck defended AI usage in Hollywood during a conversation with Bloombergs Lucas Shaw on Thursday.
Ben Affleck's son Samuel appears to have developed a taste for Lamborghinis, four years after he accidentally backed one into another luxury car.
During a recent appearance on his "Animals" co-star Kerry Washington's podcast, "Street You Grew Up On," the 54-year-old actor said that Samuel, 14, inherited his affinity for luxury items.
Affleck, who shares three children including Samuel, Violet, 20, and Fin, 17, with his ex-wife Jennifer Garner, told Washington that he recently shut down his son's request to buy him a Lamborghini.
BEN AFFLECK ADMITS HIS TEENAGER ROASTED HIS DATING HISTORY WHILE AT DINNER

"I see my son now, you know, and he's a lot like me," Affleck said. "And it makes me realize — because my older two ones — they kind of spoiled me because they're like, 'No, we don't want this. We don't want that.' They're like, aversive."
Ben Affleck shut down his 14-year-old son Samuel's request for him to buy a yellow Lamborghini. (Getty Images)

"My son's like, ‘Dad, you should get a Lambo,’" the Oscar winner recalled with a laugh. "'What? A Lambo? Are you f---ing crazy? Am I an a--hole in a yellow Lamborghini driving around like at the club?' He's like, 'Yeah.'"
ROB LOWE SAYS SON WAS MUGGED AT KNIFEPOINT AFTER IGNORING DAD'S NYC WARNING
"No. No!" Affleck exclaimed as Washington laughed.

Samuel was previously involved in a mishap with a yellow Lamborghini while visiting 777 Exotics, a luxury car rental dealership in the Los Angeles area, with his father and Affleck's then-fiancée, Jennifer Lopez, in June 2022.
At the time, Affleck allowed Samuel, then 10, to sit in the driver's seat of a bright yellow Lamborghini SUV before the boy accidentally put the car into reverse and backed into a white BMW.
Samuel accidentally backed a yellow Lamborghini into a BMW at a luxury car dealership when he was 10. (Getty Images)

Samuel was photographed jumping out of the Lamborghini to inspect the vehicles, while Affleck also checked for damage. The "Gone Girl" star was later photographed hugging Samuel while talking with Lopez, whom he married in July 2022. The former couple finalized their divorce in January 2025.
The vehicle involved in Samuel's incident was a Lamborghini Urus, which rented for $1,475 per day and was valued at $250,000 at the time, according to the New York Post.

At the time, representatives for Affleck and 777 Exotics both told the New York Post there was no damage to either vehicle. An employee at the rental dealership also said there were no hard feelings following the fender-bender.
KRISTIN CAVALLARI ADMITS HER KIDS FLY COACH WHILE SHE SITS IN FIRST CLASS
"Affleck loves cars," the dealership employee told the New York Post. "We hope they come in again."
Affleck previously refused to buy Samuel a $6,000 pair of sneakers. (Getty Images)
The Lamborghini isn't the first high-priced item to catch Samuel's eye.
In March 2025, an exchange between Affleck and Samuel made headlines after Samuel was filmed admiring a $6,000 pair of Dior x Nike Air Jordan 1 sneakers in a video shared on Instagram.
MARK WAHLBERG ADMITS HOLLYWOOD FAME COMES WITH ‘BAGGAGE’ FOR HIS KIDS

In the clip, Affleck and Samuel browsed sneakers at a convention, where Samuel spotted the Dior shoes. After seeing the $6,000 price tag, Affleck told his son, "That's a lot of lawns you gotta mow there."
During an interview with Access Hollywood later that month, Affleck joked about the viral video.
MICHAEL DOUGLAS SAYS KIRK DOUGLAS GAVE HIM $10,000 AT 21 AND TOLD HIM HE WAS ON HIS OWN
"That's what happens when you tell a motherf---er they have to mow a lawn," he told the outlet. "All of a sudden they don't want those shoes, and he was like, ‘But I always said they were tough.’"
"It's always some grift why I need to be … I'm like, 'Man, you do not need thousand-dollar shoes!' He's like, 'We have the money.' I'm like, 'I have the money, you're broke!'" Affleck quipped.

Affleck co-parents his three children with Garner, whom he was married to from 2005 to 2018. During an April 2025 appearance on "Today with Jenna & Friends," Affleck explained how he was teaching his children that they shouldn't expect handouts from their famous parents.
Affleck explained that he wants his children to understand the value of hard work.
The actor said that his children don't care about his success in Hollywood. (Reuters)

"You love your kids. You want to give them everything and do everything for them, but I think you definitely do them a disservice by not connecting [if] you want something that you want, you have to work for that," he said.
During a recent appearance on "Late Night with Seth Meyers," Affleck said that his children don't care about his Hollywood success.

"I remember when my daughter was born, right around the time I directed my first movie and I had a bunch of movies that didn't work and was very uncool and felt kind of despised and thought like, 'God, I really want to make my kids proud with my career,'" he recalled.
"And as I've gotten older, my kids have gotten older, what I realized is, they don't give a s---," he continued as the audience laughed.
"They really don't care," he added. "The most cool thing I've ever done, in my kids' eyes, is, like, become a meme."

In December 2020, Affleck was photographed struggling to carry several Dunkin' iced coffees and a box of Munchkins outside his Los Angeles home. The photos went viral and inspired memes, with social media users joking that Affleck's exasperated expression summed up the frustrations of 2020.

Affleck said that his children were more impressed by his Dunkin' Donuts meme. (Brigette Buckner/Dunkin' via AP)
Affleck later entered into an official partnership with the coffee chain in 2023, when he starred in and directed its first-ever Super Bowl commercial.
During the interview with Meyers, Affleck recalled asking his children why they were impressed by his Dunkin' meme.
"I'm like, 'Why is that cool? Like, because I'm spilling a coffee?'" he recalled. "They're like, 'You're relevant.'"

title: Sarah Ferguson rejects tell-all speculation as expert says discretion is ‘only hope’ for future with family
summary: Royal experts weigh in on Sarah Ferguson's denied memoir rumors, warning a tell-all could risk her relationship with daughters and grandchildren.
story: Royal broadcaster Ian Pelham Turner discusses Sarah Ferguson's denial of tell-all rumors and the potential consequences for daughters Princess Beatrice and Princess Eugenie.
Sarah Ferguson is setting the record straight about her intent to write a memoir.

In a statement to People, representatives for the former Duchess of York shut down claims she is gearing up to release a tell-all, telling the outlet there have been "no discussions" about a book deal.
"She is not writing a personal memoir," they said.

Rumors she was preparing to release a memoir started in late September, when The Sun reported Ferguson was "days away" from signing a lucrative book deal which would cover her ex-husband, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's relationship with Jeffrey Epstein.
Representatives for Ferguson shut down rumors she is preparing to write a tell-all memoir. (Daniele Venturelli/Getty Images)
FORMER PRINCE ANDREW, SARAH FERGUSON DUBBED ROYAL FAMILY’S ‘BONNIE AND CLYDE’ AS EPSTEIN FALLOUT GROWS: AUTHOR

"The other day it was announced by the Sun newspaper that Sarah Ferguson was attempting to write a book, an all-tell book, giving all the secrets away about the royal family. It was strongly denied very quickly by her PR team," royal broadcaster Ian Pelham Turner told Fox News Digital.

"And I think the reality was this might have been a strategy to actually gain more initiatives, but who knows? We will never know with the royal family itself. She's obviously very considerate about what might happen if a book was written like this to Eugenie and Beatrice, and also to her former husband, Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor too."

Former Prince Andrew is seen departing Westminster Abbey after the coronation ceremony of King Charles III and Queen Camilla on May 6, 2023, in London, England. The former Duke of York vacated Royal Lodge on Feb. 2, 2026. (Karwai Tang/WireImage/Getty Images)

Turner added that the book would likely not be very complimentary of Windsor, noting that she wasn't "very well treated in the formative years of her marriage with Andrew" and likely felt "lonely" and "isolated."
WATCH: SARAH FERGUSON DENIES TELL-ALL BOOK AMID ROYAL FAMILY CONCERNS: EXPERT

British royals expert Hilary Fordwich told Fox News Digital that Ferguson is "already persona-non-grata in aristocratic circles" and will be "weary" of making any decisions that will "put her daughters and grandchildren at risk of being ousted completely from the royal family."

"Sarah should simply stick to anything unrelated to the royals, her fiction & anything else without any royal proximity," Fordwich said. "But simply refraining from such wouldn’t be rehabilitation or societal acceptance. Currently, she is persona non grata."

"The only hope she has of any future, indeed also any future with her own daughters and grandchildren, is to be discreet, which is not one of her strongest virtues, to say the least. But staying out of the U.K. for the last seven months was wise to at least let things die down. But despicable behavior will never be forgotten," Fordwich added.
Royal expert, Hilary Fordwich told Fox News Digital that Ferguson is "persona non grata" in the U.K. (Stephane Cardinale - Corbis/Corbis via Getty Images)

Fordwich added that while a tell-all "would be just a quick fix for her financial woes," it would also "pretty much guarantee zero relationship with her children, grandchildren as well as her social set."

Ferguson spent seven months abroad before announcing her return to the U.K. in August, a decision Fordwich called "wise" as it allowed time for things to "die down," but added, "despicable behavior will never be forgotten."

"Sarah Ferguson is back in the U.K., keeping a low profile and plotting her next move," British broadcaster and photographer Helena Chard told Fox News Digital. "Her chequered past has led to her immense highs and lows over the years. She believes that her current situation is merely another storm in a teacup. She plans to pivot yet again and bounce back."
The controversy surrounding Ferguson stems from her association with Epstein. In the Epstein files, emails allegedly show the former royal asking the child sex offender for financial help.

title: Ella Langley says canceled concert was ‘not worth a human life’ after bomb threat
summary: Ella Langley became emotional during her Texas concert explaining why she canceled her sold-out BOK Center show despite Tulsa police finding no credible threat.
story: Country music superstar Ella Langley encouraged fans to not to measure themselves against social media or other people’s expectations during a concert performance.
Ella Langley is speaking out about her decision to cancel her concert in Tulsa, Oklahoma, following a reported bomb threat.
The 27-year-old country star addressed the cancellation while performing in Lubbock, Texas, one day after calling off her sold-out Friday night show at Tulsa's BOK Center.
Langley became emotional while explaining why she decided not to perform despite police finding no credible threat.

"I was put in charge of a decision for 15,000 people and I decided to make the decision that I could live with the rest of my life," the "Choosin' Texas" hitmaker told the crowd on Saturday night at the United Supermarkets Arena, according to Taste of Country.
Ella Langley is standing by her decision to cancel her Friday night concert in Oklahoma after a bomb threat.  (FilmMagic)

"Because when it comes to keeping you safe and making sure that this show is a safe place for us to come and enjoy our music, then it will happen," she continued. "But the second, it feels like it's not, I'm not doing it. I'm not doing it because a concert's not worth a human life. It's not."
ED SHEERAN APOLOGIZES FOR MACKLEMORE BACKLASH, ENCOURAGES UNITY AT FIRST CONCERT SINCE FALLOUT
"And so I would have made yesterday's decision ten billion times over," she added. "And I'd do it tomorrow and I'd do it the next day."
Langley went on to explain that the safety of her fans outweighed her desire to perform.
The country star said that a concert is "not worth a human life." (Getty Images for SiriusXM)

"Because while I'm grateful to get to do what I do, it's not the most important thing in this life," she said. "What's the most important thing in this life is the people around you that love you and that are there for you no matter what."
"The most important thing in this life is that you wake up every day and feel like, 'You know what, I'm good today. I am so grateful to have woken up today,'" Langley continued.
ELLA LANGLEY DELIVERS POWERFUL FAITH MESSAGE TO CROWD DURING MORGAN WALLEN CONCERT IN CHICAGO
"The most important thing in this life, number one, is your relationship with Jesus Christ," she added.

Langley admitted that she nearly canceled Saturday's concert in Texas because she was still shaken by the incident. However, she credited her faith in Jesus with giving her the courage to return to the stage.
ELLA LANGLEY GOES VIRAL WITH PASSIONATE COMMENTS ABOUT HER CHRISTIAN FAITH, GOD, LOVE AND RELIGION
"If it wasn't for Him," I would have canceled this show tonight," she told the crowd. "I would have."

"But I felt this calling and this tug in my chest saying, 'It's OK. We are safe. We can do this show,'" Langley continued. "And I decided to do it because of Him right there. And that's the only reason."
Langley shared that she almost canceled her Saturday night concert due to the scare.  (Jason Kempin/Getty Images)
ELLA LANGLEY'S FAITH AND AUTHENTICITY FUEL RECORD-BREAKING RISE, EXPERTS SAY

"I'm not gonna live in fear," Langley added. "We're going to put on music and get to do this for the rest of our lives. And I know that. I know because this is my calling. This is the thing that I was called to do, and I'm going to continue doing it. Nobody is going to take me out of it or scare me out."
Langley expressed her gratitude to her fans for coming to her Texas show despite the frightening incident at the Oklahoma concert.

"I know yesterday was scary, it was scary for all of us," she said. "But we're just so grateful to be playing this show tonight. We're so grateful and we will never take this for granted. We love it, we love what we do. I wouldn't trade it for the world."

"Tonight I can tell that y'all knew that I've needed what you've given me. And this band and this crew — you knew that we needed this show tonight, so thank you so much for giving it to us," Langley added.
ED SHEERAN'S GILLETTE STADIUM CONCERTS CALLED OFF AS TROUBLED TOUR FACES FRESH SETBACK
Langley announced the cancelation of Friday night's concert on Instagram approximately two hours before the show was scheduled to begin.
Langley announced the cancellation two hours before the show was set to begin.  (Getty Images)

"Due to a serious security threat involving the safety of my fans, the venue staff, and my team, the incredibly difficult decision was made to cancel tonight’s show. This decision was made under the advisement of local authorities, the venue, and my security team," the singer began.
She said the decision followed guidance from local authorities, venue officials and her security team, adding that she refused to put anyone in danger.

"I know how much time, travel, money, and planning goes into coming to a show, and I can’t tell you how sorry I am. This is not a decision that was made lightly. I was so looking forward to spending tonight with you, but your safety will always mean more to me than anything else. I refuse to put anyone in harm’s way," the country music star's statement concluded.

The BOK Center also released a statement on Friday. "The safety and well-being of everyone involved is our absolute priority, and after careful consideration, we have determined that the show cannot proceed. We understand the disappointment this news brings and apologize to fans who planned to attend. The safety of fans is our foremost concern and will always come first," the statement read.
The official Instagram account for the BOK Center said that ticket refunds and additional information will be shared as soon as possible.

Langley's explanation for her decision to cancel the concert comes after the Tulsa Police Department said that they found no credible threat to the event.

In a since-deleted statement posted to Facebook, the department explained that officers had conducted routine security sweeps before the concert using K-9 units, bomb technicians, patrol officers and venue security personnel and "did not find anything" dangerous.

"A call was made threatening the lives of people attending the event," they continued. Actress Lesley-Anne Down plays former U.K. Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher in the biopic "Reagan." (Rawhide Pictures)

"I remember there was a little girl, one of a number of children who were murdered and buried on the moors in England," the British star told Fox News Digital. "There was a little girl who had dark hair and blue eyes and was my age, 10. Her name was Leslie Ann Downey. My mother got phone calls when this little girl's identity was announced."

"It wasn't me, of course," said Down. "But it certainly freaked her out. Leslie Ann Downey was about six months younger than me. It turned out there were two people, a man and a woman. Ian Brady and Myra Hindley. They were the killers."
Lesley Ann Downey, age 10, one of the children murdered by Ian Brady and Myra Hindley, is shown in a photo. (Mirrorpix via Getty Images)

Brady and Hindley murdered five children between 1963 and 1965, with several of their victims buried on Saddleworth Moor in northern England, according to The Associated Press. The case became known as the Moors murders.
WATCH: ‘REAGAN’ PRODUCER SHARES WHAT HE LEARNED FROM RESEARCHING RONALD REAGAN

Hindley and Brady were arrested in 1965 and later convicted of murders connected to the case. The five victims were Downey, Pauline Reade, John Kilbride, Keith Bennett and Edward Evans, who ranged in age from 10 to 17. Bennett's body has never been found.
Ian Brady and Myra Hindley were found guilty of murder in Chester, England, on May 6, 1966. Both were sentenced to life imprisonment. (Bettmann Archive)
According to accounts of the case, Downey was abducted after Hindley asked her to help carry packages to a car.
Hindley died in 2002 while serving a life sentence. Brady died in a psychiatric hospital in 2017.

Floral tributes overlook Saddleworth Moor in Saddleworth, United Kingdom, where the body of missing Keith Bennett may be buried. Bennett was abducted by moors murderers Ian Brady and Myra Hindley on June 16, 1964, and they never disclosed his burial location. (Getty Images)
The case frightened Down’s family. But it wouldn’t be the last time danger came close to home.

"A year later, my mother and I were coming back from the launderette with the washing," Down said. "I ran ahead. I left the washing, I left my mother and just ran ahead. I ran uphill and then over a footbridge. As I ran over the footbridge, a man came from the other side. He's walking towards me. He stops in the middle of the footbridge and says, 'Hello.' He then was going to put me in his car."
Harrison Ford and Lesley-Anne Down on the set of "Hanover Street," written and directed by Peter Hyams. (Corbis via Getty Images)

"He told me he needed a babysitter, and he would call my parents when we got to his house," Down said. "I remember having one foot in the car. Seeing my mother broke the spell. Then he was gone. But I still remember that horrible feeling swooping in before my mother came."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
English actress Lesley-Anne Down took on the role of Margaret Thatcher in the 2024 biopic "Reagan." (BSR Agency)
Years later, when Down was 18, she ordered a taxi. But when a car pulled up in the countryside, she climbed in and quickly noticed something was wrong.

"As soon as he's driving away, I'm already feeling that horrible feeling," Down said. "I looked around and there were no radios or anything, like a taxi is supposed to have. So I said, 'Could you pull over, please?' He said, 'Oh no, we don't need to pull over. We'll be there soon.'"
Patrick Swayze and Lesley-Anne Down appear in the TV miniseries "North and South," circa 1985. (Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)
Down said she decided to jump from the moving car.
Lesley-Anne Down poses for a portrait in New York circa 1980. (Getty Images)

"I opened the door and threw myself out of the 25-mile an hour car," she said. "I fell onto the curb in a puddle. I was covered in blood. There was nobody around. What did he do? He pulled the car door shut and drove off at top speed. I didn't freeze up because I couldn't. That feeling was familiar to me. I've been through it."

Down, now 72, earned a Golden Globe nomination for her role opposite Patrick Swayze in "North and South." She also starred opposite Peter Sellers in "The Pink Panther Strikes Again" and Harrison Ford in "Hanover Street." She later appeared on the soap opera "The Bold and the Beautiful."
Lesley-Anne Down as Madeline Fabray LaMotte Main in the TV miniseries 'North and South,' 1985. (Getty Images)
When asked what advice she would give to women pursuing a career in Hollywood, Down had a warning: "Never go anywhere alone."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Lesley-Anne Down, a British actress, is pictured at home in Primrose Hill, London, on Wednesday, Oct. 4, 1972. (Getty Images)

"Always have your agent or your publicist with you at all times," she said. "Even if they have to be on the phone a lot and out in the lobby, just always have somebody with you at all times as you chase your dreams."

"I made a decision many, many years ago, actually about 2012, that I wanted out," Down said. "I was in a position where I didn't have to. Things were very good. And I was fortunate to have all my eggs in a basket and make a choice."
Lesley-Anne Down attends the 6,000th episode of "The Bold and the Beautiful" at CBS Television City in Los Angeles on Feb. 7, 2011. (FilmMagic)
Down has since moved from California to Georgia. She also said she has no regrets about turning down two opportunities to play a Bond girl.
Sean Connery and Lesley-Anne Down in a scene from the 1979 film "The Great Train Robbery." (Getty Images)

"I guess my thought process was maybe a little old-fashioned, but being a Bond girl didn't really resonate with me," she explained. "Being a Bond girl was skimpy clothing, pretty face, not much dialogue, no acting involved, kissing James at the end in a spacecraft or whatever. I thought if I became a Bond girl, then I'd be a Bond girl for life. I didn't want that for myself."
The opportunity to play Thatcher came "out of the blue," Down said. She accepted the role and said she was grateful for the experience.
Lesley Anne-Down attends The Hollywood Show held at the Westin LAX Hotel in Los Angeles on Feb. 10, 2018. (WireImage)
"She loved and believed in England and the English people," Down said. "Her counterpart, Mr. Reagan, also believed and loved the American people."

The director's cut of "Reagan" was released on Sept. 25, 2026. (Rawhide Pictures)
Down said leaders should "encompass what Thatcher and Reagan both believed," including doing "anything and everything they can for the longevity and success of the nation."

For Down, taking on the role of Thatcher became another unexpected chapter in a life that has repeatedly taken surprising turns. But these days, the actress is content with where those turns have taken her.

Margaret Thatcher, British Prime Minister, addresses a Press Conference at Conservative Party Headquarters in Smith Square, London on June 8, 1987, during the General Election campaign. (David Levenson/Getty Images)
"My choice was to live the life I’m living now," she said.

title: Kelly Clarkson slams Brooklyn store over ‘Pretty Woman’ treatment
summary: Kelly Clarkson claims a Brooklyn store employee treated her like she couldn't afford the merchandise, comparing the experience to "Pretty Woman."
story: Steve Summers, Dolly Parton's creative director, joins Martha MacCallum on 'The Story' to discuss the opening of the 'Life of Many Colors Museum' and hotel in Nashville, Tennessee. The projects celebrate the legendary singer's rags-to-rhinestones legacy. Fans express emotional reactions to the immersive experience, sharing how they can feel her presence throughout the new building.
Kelly Clarkson is calling out a Brooklyn store after she claimed an employee mistreated her.
On Saturday, the singer and talk show host took to X to share details of her recent experience at Art of Play, a store known for its collection of toys, games, books, puzzles and other unique items.

"Just drove all the way to Brooklyn to check out this store I thought looked really rad and had a few things in mind to buy and literally was looked at as if I couldn’t afford it and was told he could find something comparable for me," Clarkson wrote.
KELLY CLARKSON WON’T LET HER KIDS WATCH ‘FROM JUSTIN TO KELLY’ AFTER BRUTAL ADMISSION ABOUT 2003 FILM
Kelly Clarkson described a recent shopping experience to one of Julia Roberts' character in "Pretty Woman." (Getty Images)
"Wow, dude. You’re an idiot and just lost a huge sale," she continued.

Clarkson then compared the encounter to a memorable scene from the 1990 film "Pretty Woman," in which Julia Roberts’ character, Vivian Ward, is dismissed by a boutique saleswoman who assumes she cannot afford the store’s clothing.
MICHAEL DOUGLAS' WILDEST HOLLYWOOD CONFESSIONS: FROM A-LIST ACTRESS BITE TO JULIA ROBERTS CLASH
"But y’all should go check out Art of Play in Brooklyn if you enjoy being treated like Julia Roberts’ character in ‘Pretty Woman.’ For sure, check it out," Clarkson added.
The singer’s description of the incident echoed the famous "Pretty Woman" scene, in which Vivian returns to the boutique after being rejected and tells the saleswoman, "Big mistake. Big. Huge."

Clarkson’s post quickly drew attention from her followers, some of whom defended the singer and criticized the store on social media. Several users also appeared to leave negative reviews on the business’ Google listing.
The singer called out Art of Play in Brooklyn for allegedly mistreating her. (Getty Images for The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame)
KELLY CLARKSON WON’T LET HER KIDS WATCH ‘FROM JUSTIN TO KELLY’ AFTER BRUTAL ADMISSION ABOUT 2003 FILM
One Yelp reviewer wrote, "Rude!!!! If I could give zero I would! Treat people like you want to be treated walking into a store."
Art of Play so far has not issued a formal statement addressing Clarkson’s claims.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
However, the store appeared to respond indirectly by sharing an Instagram Story featuring a customer review praising the staff’s "genuine kindness," according to Us Weekly.
"From the very first time I walked into @artofplay, I felt welcomed and treated with such genuine kindness," the review stated.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Clarkson's alleged encounter prompted chatter online. (Weiss Eubanks/NBCUniversal via Getty Images)
The customer added that Art of Play was "a place that leaves you smiling and wanting to come back."
The Instagram Story was later deleted, according to the outlet.
The store posted a statement about Clarkson to their Instagram page on Sunday afternoon.

"Yesterday, Kelly Clarkson visited us in Brooklyn and inquired about buying "Molly," a one-of-a-kind singing and dancing bird automaton who plays an important role in the magic shows we host here. Molly is permanently attached to the wall and isn’t for sale," the store wrote.

Adding: "However, the negative experience Kelly described on twitter would resonate with anyone who has ever felt judged in a shop. At Art of Play whether someone comes in to make a purchase or simply look around for a while, they are equally welcome. We greet everyone who walks in the door with the invitation to "pick things up and play." And they do, many stay for hours enjoying our puzzles, games and toys."

"Imagine our surprise when our small local business was suddenly attacked by 8 million people who have never visited our store. It’s been a surreal experience to be the focus of such widespread outrage after just one mention by a celebrity. Thanks to all our friends for their support and welcome to all the curious folks who discovered us amidst the drama. We’re going to keep our heads down and hopefully, we can clear things up with Kelly someday. As a talented popular singer once said "what doesn’t kill you makes you stronger."
After the store's Instagram post, Clarkson took to her X account and Instagram stories on Sunday afternoon to respond to their claims.
"Cool, cool. Sure, it wasn't for sale. That's the narrative Art of Play is gonna go with," Clarkson wrote, adding a thumbs up emoji.

The singer continued: "So the whole conversation we had when I asked you if it was for sale whilst pointing to the price tag hanging on the wall with the title Singing Bird didn't happen as you elevator eyed me saying in a condescending tone "yes, it’s for sale but it costs 15,000 dollars so if you’d like me to find something comparable for you I can." That all never happened and now it’s not for sale. Okay, cool. So you’re not only rude, you’re also a liar. Got it," adding a checkmark emoji.

Clarkson added: "And by the way, I obviously support small businesses because I was literally at a small business trying to purchase things. I love small businesses and know they are important and I always support them, but you don’t get a free pass to treat people less than in your store just because you are a small business. It’s not that hard to be kind. I never blast people but you my friend were an exception. Your store is really cool. Unfortunately, you aren’t."

The star also added a photo which included what appeared to be an alleged price tag for the item circled in red. The photo had the caption: "Molly’s not for sale yet has a $15,000 price tag. Kelly Clarkson you will always be a real one."
MICHAEL DOUGLAS' WILDEST HOLLYWOOD CONFESSIONS: FROM A-LIST ACTRESS BITE TO JULIA ROBERTS CLASH

The back and forth didn't end there. Art of Play took to social media to "clarify one additional detail" about Clarkson's visit. "During the 5 minutes she spent in the store, she inquired about our mechanical bird puppet named Molly. We explained that while Molly is permanently attached to the wall and serves as a de facto mascot for our shop, a nearly identical automaton is owned by the creator of the machines, a brilliant artist named Bliss Kolb who lives in Seattle. He told us he would be willing to part with Molly’s twin for $15,000. We explained all of this to Kelly Clarkson."

"We also offered to show her a different singing bird automaton, made by a traditional clockmaking shop in Germany, that she could have taken home with her that day. It costs about $2,000. She did not stick around long enough to see it."
"We’ve reached out to Kelly directly to try and clear the air," the shop concluded. "We really do wish her the best and hope that someday we can all laugh about this misunderstanding."
A representative for Art of Play did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

title: Elon Musk's mom Maye nearly turned down SI Swimsuit cover over 'wrinkles and cellulite'
summary: Maye Musk nearly turned down her Sports Illustrated Swimsuit cover over wrinkle fears, but a phone call from her daughter changed everything.
story: Author Maye Musk joins Fox & Friends to discuss her new memoir "Timeless." She shares her story of escaping a toxic marriage, raising three children as a single mother and finding career success after 50.
Maye Musk nearly passed on the chance to make a splash in Sports Illustrated Swimsuit because she worried about looking "wrinkly" in the iconic magazine.

The Canadian-born, South African-raised model made history in 2022 as the oldest Sports Illustrated Swimsuit cover model at 74. Martha Stewart later broke the record at 81 in 2023. Now, Musk is looking back at the milestone and her journey from a single mother of three to a sought-after model in her new book, "Timeless."

"At my age, you have wrinkles and cellulite on your arms and on your thighs, so I prefer to wear long sleeves," the mother of tech mogul Elon Musk told Fox News Digital. "So, the idea of wearing a swimsuit was very uncomfortable. But then my daughter called me. I told her they were going to be shooting in Belize. She instantly said, 'You've got to go. Belize is beautiful.' So, I did. I took a chance."
MAYE MUSK DEFENDS SYDNEY SWEENEY'S NUDE SPORTS AD AND RECALLS 12-YEAR PATH TO CITIZENSHIP

Canadian-South African model Maye Musk arrives for the screening of the film "Asteroid City" during the 76th edition of the Cannes Film Festival in Cannes, on May 23, 2023. Musk has written a new book, "Timeless." (Patricia De Melo Moreira/AFP via Getty Images)

In the book, Musk wrote, "I was still 73. My skin showed the signs of my weight having cycled up and down so many times in my life, including for each of my pregnancies. I'm wrinkly and I have cellulite. Swimsuit model?"
Despite her worries, Musk said she felt at ease when she began posing for photographer Yu Tsai. She even wore colorful two-pieces for the occasion.
Fox News may be compensated for or earn a commission if you buy through our referral links.
Maye Musk is seen here posing for the 2022 Sports Illustrated swimsuit issue cover on Jan. 29, 2022, in Belize (Yu Tsai/Sports Illustrated via Contour RA by Getty Images)

"It was very unusual," she said with a laugh. "I've been told all of my life that I'm not a swimsuit model. When you think of swimsuit models, you think of the Victoria's Secret models. Those are really special body shapes. So it was a challenge for me. But as I say, you have to take a chance in life. And I knew they're not going to publish ugly photos. At one point, I felt so at ease that I even started dancing with the local people. I was in awe of exploring a new country, a new culture. That's what I love doing. And I got to celebrate me."
WATCH: MAYE MUSK DISCUSSES RAISING ELON MUSK, ESCAPING TOXIC MARRIAGE IN NEW MEMOIR ‘TIMELESS’
Looking back, Musk said she wonders why she was so nervous.

"When women go to the beach, they wrap a towel around themselves," she said. "But men, they could be obese, and they're still strutting in Speedos with such confidence. We really have to make a change. And if any man insults your body, well, they can get lost. There's always going to be somebody who feels the need to trash on you. It's not fair. But it's all about embracing who you are and not apologizing for that."
Maye Musk's book "Timeless: The Art of Reinvention and Resilience at Any Age" is available now. (Harper Wave)
Musk didn't undergo a makeover to appear younger for the cover. Her signature silver hair remained untouched.
Maye Musk attends the launch of the 2025 Sports Illustrated Swimsuit issue at Hard Rock Hotel New York on May 15, 2025, in New York City. (Getty Images for Sports Illustrated Swimsuit)

"Why do I need to color my hair?" Musk said. "You have to do the roots every four weeks, and I used to do them myself. Your hair then becomes very brittle because it's so damaged. And it grows out. And then I decided to cut my hair short. Soon after, I had four billboards in Times Square. I didn't feel like a granny. I felt fashionable."
It wasn't the first time Musk took a chance on a modeling gig.

From left: Christie Brinkley, Maye Musk, Brooks Nader, Kate Love, Kate Upton and Lily Aldridge attend the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Celebration of the 2024 Issue Release and 60th Anniversary with Swimsuit Island in Hollywood, Florida, on May 17, 2024. (Getty Images for Sports Illustrated Swimsuit)
In her book, Musk describes a phone call she received from her agent: "Tomorrow, you pose naked for the cover of TIME magazine. You're the only model they want and they won't budge."
Musk had never done a nude shoot because, as she wrote, "nobody had ever asked."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Maye Musk, an author and dietician, also has campaigns with high-profiled brands like CoverGirl and Dior Beauty. (Fadil Berisha)
Before stripping down, Musk sought advice from her children.

"I picked up the phone to dial Elon first, then stopped myself," Musk wrote. "I already knew what he would say: 'Absolutely not.' He was not the kind of son who wanted his mother naked on magazine covers. Not prudish, but definitely more conservative when it came to nudity. So I called Tosca. I wasn't too surprised to find that she was not in love with the idea, either. 'You never do naked!' she said. Her instinct was protective, not wanting me to risk an uncomfortable experience."
Maye Musk and Elon Musk attend the 2022 Met Gala celebrating "In America: An Anthology of Fashion" at the Metropolitan Museum of Art on May 2, 2022, in New York City. (Getty Images)

"Finally, I called Kimbal," she wrote. "Of my three children, he is the most relaxed and free-spirited. (He met his current wife at Burning Man.) He had a completely different perspective. ‘It’s TIME magazine. It’s journalism,’ he said. ‘Not some nudie magazine. It’ll be tasteful. You have nothing to worry about. Do it.’"
Musk told Fox News Digital it was important for her to get her children's approval before posing nude.
Maye Musk walks the runway at the Philipp Plein fashion show during Milan Fashion Week Womenswear Fall/Winter 2023/2024 on Feb. 25, 2023, in Milan, Italy. (Getty Images)
"Well, would you want your mother naked on the front cover of a magazine?" she said.

"But it was Kimbal who encouraged me. He said it would be tasteful. He's always been a free spirit. And I trust him. When I arrived for the photoshoot, they were very careful with me. You have a makeup artist who has to go through your whole body. Then they did my hair and very plain makeup. Then they sat me with a mirror in front of me, so I could see exactly what the photographer sees."
From left: Kimbal Musk, his mother Maye Musk and his wife Christiana Musk attend the Kering Foundation Caring For Women Dinner in New York City. (Getty Images)

"The photographer came in for the shoot, and maybe five minutes later, it was over," she said. "It was really quick and very respectful. They immediately brought a robe for me. I got changed and went home. That's all there was to it."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Maye Musk attends the Sports Illustrated Swim Issue Launch Party at the Hard Rock Hotel on May 16, 2024, in New York. (WWD via Getty Images)

For Musk, aging with confidence isn't just about embracing wrinkles and silver hair. The longtime dietitian also believes that taking care of your health plays an important role in feeling your best at any age.
Maye Musk attends the Juzui FW25 Collection show at The Glasshouse in New York City on Feb. 7, 2025. (Getty Images for Juzui)

"It gets harder to lose weight as you get older," Musk said. "With my patients, I always tell them to plan ahead. If you get hungry, there's no salad next to you. There's a donut. Also, only eat when you're hungry. And when you are hungry, make sure there is healthy food around, no desserts or chocolates. And if my patient didn't take the journey seriously, I would tell them, 'You can't come anymore.'"
From left: Tosca Musk and her mother Maye Maye Musk attend the "Downton Abbey: The Grand Finale" New York premiere at Jazz at Lincoln Center on Sept. 8, 2025. (WireImage)

"Even 10 pounds can make you feel uncomfortable," she said. "Everything is tight and you don't have confidence. You have to track your food intake. If a patient goes off what I recommended, they need to explain why. You need to hold yourself accountable if you want to make smarter choices for your health."
Maye Musk attends the launch of the 2022 Sports Illustrated Swimsuit issue and debut of Pay With Change at Hard Rock Hotel New York on May 19, 2022. (Getty Images)
Musk said each decade of her life has been better than the last. At 78, she's happily embracing aging and hopes other women will do the same.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Maye Musk visits "Fox & Friends" at Fox News Channel Studios in New York City on Sept. 18, 2026. (Getty Images)

"When my mom was 86, she moved from South Africa to Canada and started all over," Musk said. "She was an artist. When she was nearing 90, her hands weren't strong enough to do the wood carvings she loved. So, by 94, she started doing computer art. My older sister taught her. She died at 98. But she always remained curious and busy. She was always exploring."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

From left: Maye Musk, Christen Harper, Hailey Clauson and Georgina Burke attend the Swimsuit on Location event hosted by Sports Illustrated Swimsuit at Hard Rock Seminole in Hollywood, Florida, on May 21, 2022. (Getty Images for Sports Illustrated Swimsuit)

"You're never too old to start again," Musk said. "And don't worry about the wrinkles. A man doesn't care if he gets wrinkles. He still has his confidence. When you get insecure, you become less attractive. I didn't do anything to my face because I wanted to frown and have expression. But also, don't mix with people who make you feel insecure. They're not your friends. And there will be people who will push you down. You can't stay down. You just have to get up and show your talents, who you are."
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Prince Edward told girlfriend he wanted 'two wives' before marrying royal family's 'secret weapon': memoir
summary: Ruthie Henshall claims in her memoir that Prince Edward once told her he wished he could have two wives before marrying Sophie, Duchess of Edinburgh.
story: Royal historian Hugo Vickers, who wrote a new book on the late monarch, explains how the Queen Mother favored another suitor, but Queen Elizabeth ultimately chose Prince Philip.
Before Prince Edward married his royal family's "secret weapon," he once told an ex-girlfriend he wished he could have two wives, according to her new memoir.

Years earlier, the youngest son of the late Queen Elizabeth II dated actress Ruthie Henshall from 1988 to 1993. The West End star recently opened up about their romance in her memoir "The Showgirl and the Prince."

"Ruth, I couldn't put you through the job," Henshall recalled Edward telling her. "If I could, I would have two wives. One for the job, and one whom I loved, because you would never want to subject the woman you love to the job."
QUEEN ELIZABETH’S MOTHER WANTED HER TO MARRY ANOTHER MAN BEFORE PRINCE PHILIP: AUTHOR
Prince Edward's former flame, actress Ruthie Henshall, has written a memoir about their past romance. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images; David M. Benett/Getty Images)
Fox News Digital reached out to Henshall, 59, and Edward, 62, for comment. A Buckingham Palace spokesperson previously told Fox News Digital the palace doesn't comment on books.

The pair first met in 1988 while Henshall was starring in "Cats" and Edward was working as a production assistant for Andrew Lloyd Webber's Really Useful Theatre Company. Henshall recalled making a beeline for the young prince when he arrived at the theater, playfully welcoming him "to the litter." A romance blossomed.
Fox News may be compensated for or earn a commission if you buy through our referral links.
"The Showgirl and the Prince" by Ruthie Henshall is available now. (Macmillan Publishers)
As their relationship grew more serious, Henshall said the realities of royal life began to set in.
WATCH: WHY QUEEN ELIZABETH REJECTED HER MOTHER'S PREFERRED MATCH: AUTHOR

"Honestly, this type of thinking is very standard for royal men throughout history," royal commentator Amanda Matta told Fox News Digital. "It's why royal mistresses were so common. For most of history, official marriages have been strategic and political arrangements. But the royals are still people, and they need intimacy and companionship like anyone else."
"Edward and Sophie have been married for over 25 years though and seem genuinely well-matched," Matta added.
Prince Edward, Duke of Edinburgh and Sophie, Duchess of Edinburgh attend Day 2 of the Royal Windsor Horse Show in Home Park at Windsor Castle in Windsor, England, on May 2, 2024. (Getty Images)
Royal broadcaster Ian Pelham Turner told Fox News Digital it's easy to see why the prince was drawn to Henshall.
Actress Ruthie Henshall poses at a photocall for the Broadway musical "She Loves Me," date unknown. (PA Images via Getty Images)

"Ruthie Henshall has been a renowned theatre actress for several decades and Edward loved that world," he explained. "I personally remember working with the National Youth Music Theatre of which Edward was president, so Ruthie would have been his ideal partner at the time."

"The relationship went on for quite a while, and she was very nervous meeting the royal family, especially the queen," Turner said. "She forgot to curtsy to her. She also saw first-hand how the royal family operated with all their high jinks behind the scenes. I feel, although she felt deeply fond of Edward, she realized she could not marry him and still have her beloved career, which was her main passion."
Prince Edward during the wedding of Prince Andrew and Sarah Ferguson on July 23, 1986, in London. (WireImage)
In the book, Henshall wrote that, at least initially, she believed love might be enough to overcome the rigid expectations of marrying into the royal family.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Ruthie Henshall, as Marguerite, and Julian Ovenden, as Armand, perform in "Marguerite" at the Theatre Royal Haymarket in London. (Corbis via Getty Images)

"Of course, I had spotted some etiquette dilemmas, but typically I'd just assumed that I'd be able to break the rules," Henshall wrote. "That an exception would be made for me. I knew how to be a good girl, but I also knew that the possibility of me going out on a wild night and flashing my boobs in public was quite high. So, there were times when I felt torn about it all, but as far as I was concerned, I just wanted him."
Matta suggested Henshall would have adapted to royal life rather than challenged its traditions.
Diana, Princess of Wales, Prince Charles (left) and Prince Edward (right) visit Wanganui Collegiate in Wanganui, New Zealand, during the Royal Tour of New Zealand on April 22, 1983. (Getty Images)

"I don't think Henshall would have shaken up the institution very much," Matta said. "Growing up British, she would have understood the monarchy and grasped the weight of its traditions in a way a true outsider or foreigner might not. In that sense, she's similar to Edward himself. He has a big personality and a real love of the art world, but he's also deeply dutiful."
Ruthie Henshall is seen here performing on stage. (Redferns)
"I suspect that, if she'd married him, she would have adapted to the role rather than reinvented it. That may have even meant giving up her career, as Sophie later had to do."
Henshall wrote that she even turned to Sarah Ferguson, who was then married to the former Prince Andrew, for guidance.
Sarah Ferguson and Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor are seen here on their wedding day in 1986. (Derek Hudson/Getty Images)
"One time when I was pining for Edward, I remember saying to Sarah, 'Would I ever be allowed to marry him?'" Henshall wrote.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Sarah Ferguson, later Duchess of York, is surrounded by press photographers as she arrives for work in Mayfair, London, on March 3, 1986, shortly after the announcement of her engagement to Prince Andrew. (David Levenson/Getty Images)

"She probably knew there wasn't a chance in hell, but still kindly said she didn't know. Later, in her memoir, she described how she wanted to make any other woman coming into the royal family feel comfortable. And she absolutely did that. She made it her mission. So, I think I got the best side of her. And I was grateful to her on many occasions."

title: 'Happy Days' star Anson Williams says he had to create a second career because sitcom pay wasn't enough
summary: Anson Williams reveals how conversations with David Cassidy and Barry Williams inspired him to pitch a musical act on the iconic sitcom.
story: ‘Happy Days’ star Anson Williams recalled how the sitcom was facing cancelation before it ‘exploded’ and became the number one most-watched show in America.
When playing Potsie Weber on "Happy Days" didn't pay well enough, actor Anson Williams came up with a side hustle: a music career.
In a recent interview on the "Still Here Hollywood Podcast," the 77-year-old actor revealed the singing sideline was simply a matter of 1970s economics.

"On 'Happy Days' we didn't have the same salaries they have today. Not even close," he said. "Nine hundred dollars an episode, $1,200 an episode. It was fine back then, but...it's not a lifetime of earnings there."

Williams said that after speaking to "Partridge Family" star David Cassidy and Barry Williams, of "The Brady Bunch," about how much money they were making by taking their singing acts off the show, he thought to himself, "Wait a minute. I sing. If I can convince Garry to put a band on the show, maybe I can get booked, and maybe I can get some extra income."
Williams shared he pitched the idea for him to sing on the show in order to make more money. (Michael Buckner/Penske Media via Getty Images)
‘BRADY BUNCH’ CAST MADE NEARLY NOTHING FROM DECADES OF RERUNS, EVE PLUMB CLAIMS

After speaking with the show's creator, Garry Marshall, about the possibility of putting together a band to perform at Arnold's, the burger joint where Fonzie held court, the legendary director gave him a chance. Marshall told him he would have to pick a song and sing it to a bulldog, telling him, "If you're good, I get laughs. If you're bad, I get laughs. You're going to sing the bulldog."

"So I do it and then the letters start coming in, and he goes 'The people like it. The people like it.' He goes, 'We'll do more. You're in charge of it though,'" Williams recalled. "Then I got a major agent for that and started getting booked at state fairs for 10 years."
Williams added that his idea to sing on the show "started this whole career" that ended up being better for him monetarily, and was "just a whole other life experience."

After finding success as a musician as well as an actor, Williams said that Marshall approached him to express how proud he was of the actor, telling him, "You found an opportunity, and you're helping the show."
Williams previously shared with Fox News Digital that the show was on the verge of being cancelled. (ABC Photo Archives/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)

During an interview with Fox News Digital in March 2024, Williams revealed that while the show started as a hit with audiences, landing in the top 15 or 20, it slid down to 48th place at one point and was "on the verge of getting canceled."

"And Garry Marshall and Jerry Paris, our director, thought, ‘What if we changed the whole tone? What if we make it a live audience sitcom?’" Williams recalled. "So, half the season, one camera. The next season, one camera. The next season — two and a half in — they switch it to live audience. And the chemistry of the cast, the writing, was magic. That's the year we went to No. 1 in the world. That's when we exploded."

When the show became a huge success, Williams recalled Marshall advising him and his young co-stars to use their platforms for good, telling them to take the spotlight they found themselves in and "shine it on people that deserve it."

Following his time on "Happy Days," Williams pivoted to working more as a writer and director. He directed episodes of "Beverly Hills, 90210," "Sabrina the Teenage Witch," "Lizzie McGuire," "Charmed," "The Secret Life of an American Teenager" and more.

title: Doctors may be getting childhood obesity wrong, new research suggests
summary: A Lancet Commission definition of clinical obesity cuts pediatric rates sharply by requiring evidence of health complications beyond body mass index.
story: Murdoch Children's Research Insitute pediatrician Dr. Danielle Longmore discusses a new global childhood obesity definition from the Murdoch Children's Research Institute that looks beyond BMI. Longmore explains how the new definition considers critical health impacts.
A new global definition of childhood obesity is reframing how doctors evaluate youth health, looking past traditional body mass index (BMI) measurements to focus on actual physiological impacts.

According to research from the Murdoch Children's Research Institute in Australia, just 2.1% to 4.9% of children and adolescents qualify as clinically obese under the revised standard, compared to 7% to 10.8% under standard BMI calculations.
Dr. Danielle Longmore, a pediatrician at the Melbourne institute, outlined the shift during an appearance on "Fox & Friends."
YOUR WAISTLINE COULD REVEAL A HIDDEN HEART RISK YOUR BMI MISSES, MAJOR STUDY FINDS

"There's a push to really understand the impact of body fat on health," Longmore said. "BMI is really just measuring size. So, it doesn't really have a way of capturing whether somebody is well or unwell."
The traditional BMI measurement calculates a person's weight relative to their height.
While clinical obesity rates are substantially lower in youth, they surge with age, peaking at 52% among adults aged 65 to 74 as chronic conditions accumulate. (iStock)

The new definition, developed by an international panel of medical experts convened by the medical journal The Lancet, requires evidence of both excess body fat and related health problems or limitations in daily activities.
WEIGHT GAIN IN CERTAIN DECADE OF LIFE MAY BE MORE DANGEROUS, STUDY SUGGESTS
These indicators can range from elevated blood pressure and abnormal blood sugar to impaired mobility or poor sleep.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
Longmore noted that many children defined as obese by BMI metrics are active, sleeping well, attending school and otherwise healthy.
The new diagnostic model formalizes what many pediatricians already practice by assessing blood pressure, blood sugar, sleep and physical mobility alongside size. (iStock)

"I think this definition just really clarifies what people have been doing in actual clinical practice," Longmore said, noting that physicians typically evaluate patients for underlying complications rather than relying strictly on scale weight.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
While clinical obesity appears to be significantly less prevalent in youth under the new model, the trajectory reverses dramatically later in life.
The study, which analyzed nearly 800,000 individuals across their lifespan, found that clinical obesity rates climbed through adulthood.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
Among adults ages 65 to 74, the rate of clinical obesity reached 52%, as health problems linked to excess body fat became more common with age.
The findings come at a time when prescription weight loss medications, particularly GLP-1 receptor agonists, are gaining in popularity.
Many children categorized as obese by traditional BMI standards are fit, active and otherwise healthy, without secondary medical complications. (iStock)
However, Longmore cautioned that the study's dataset reflects pre-GLP-1 records, making the long-term impact of these treatments an open area for future study.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"This is really just the start of understanding what this new diagnostic entity means, and we really need more research," Longmore said, emphasizing that while the definition refines clinical diagnoses, early health interventions and lifestyle prevention remain critical for children at risk.

title: Biggest waste of money in your home gym may surprise you, fitness expert says
summary: Fitness coach Jacob Zemer reveals the three home gym essentials — bands, dumbbells and a bench — that let you train every muscle group on a budget.
story: New York-based fitness coach Jacob Zemer spoke with Fox News Digital about the most worthwhile investments for working out at home — and which equipment may not deliver enough bang for the buck.
Americans are spending more on health and wellness, research shows — and for some home gym enthusiasts, the cost can quickly climb into the thousands.
A YouGov poll conducted in September 2026 found that 31% of Americans are spending more on health and wellness than a year ago, while 20% expect to spend more in the coming year.
Meanwhile, a 2026 poll by Garage Gym Experiment, an online community for home fitness enthusiasts, found that 44% of respondents expected to spend at least $1,000 on their home gyms this year.
FITNESS EXPERT REVEALS 6 THINGS PEOPLE OVER 35 SHOULD DO AFTER WORKOUTS TO STAY STRONG
But building an effective home gym doesn’t have to break the bank, according to New York-based fitness coach Jacob Zemer.
The biggest home gym money-waster may not be a particular piece of equipment, he said, but rather anything that takes up significant space and is difficult to set up or use consistently.
Building an effective home gym doesn’t have to break the bank, according to New York-based fitness coach Jacob Zemer, right. (Jacob Zemer)
Zemer spoke with Fox News Digital about the most worthwhile investments for working out at home — and which equipment may not deliver enough bang for the buck.
The 3 home gym essentials
"A lot of people think building a home gym requires an elaborate setup, and it doesn't," Zemer said.
If someone is building a home gym from scratch, the fitness pro recommends starting with a few affordable pieces and adding equipment over time.
10-MINUTE FITNESS HABIT CAN HELP ADULTS OVER 40 MAINTAIN MUSCLE AND STAY STRONG
"You can accomplish everything for every muscle group with just three items," he said.
Exercise bands are a good first investment, Zemer said, "just because they're so incredibly affordable."
They’re also very effective, he said, especially for those who are new to strength training.
Exercise bands are a good first investment, Zemer said, "just because they're so incredibly affordable." (Jacob Zemer)
"You can do everything you need to with just those pieces of equipment — and you can travel with them, bring them on a plane and to a hotel, which makes them very versatile," Zemer said.
When choosing dumbbells, it’s important to consider how much floor space they’ll take up — especially if the home gym is in a room with multiple purposes, according to Zemer.
"With adjustable dumbbells, you can have a very small floor print — however, they are a little bit more costly, and some of them are slightly fragile, so just be mindful of that," he advised.
4 SIMPLE HABITS CAN HELP SLOW MUSCLE LOSS AS YOU AGE, FITNESS EXPERT SAYS
Beginners should first focus on learning the proper form and choosing a weight that makes the final repetitions challenging, according to Zemer.
Progress doesn’t always mean moving to heavier dumbbells, he noted.
When choosing dumbbells, it’s important to consider how much floor space they’ll take up — especially if the home gym is in a room with multiple purposes, according to Zemer. (Jacob Zemer)
"Pushing yourself doesn’t mean adding 20 pounds — it could mean doing one more rep," Zemer said. "You need to progressively get stronger, because your body will adapt to the stimulus you’re using."
Once it becomes easy to complete a high number of repetitions, it may be time to increase the weight.
With some exercises, it can be limiting if you have to lie on the floor or stand, Zemer said.
"You can get quite an affordable bench online," he said. "I would look for one that both declines and inclines, maybe even perhaps sits completely upright. That will give you a lot of versatility."
For added versatility, Zemer suggests looking for a bench that both declines and inclines, and maybe even sits completely upright. (Jacob Zemer)
The biggest waste: equipment you won’t use
Before buying a piece of home gym equipment, Zemer recommends considering how much space it requires, how many exercises it supports and whether it will be easy to use consistently.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
Equipment that is bulky or difficult to move, or requires too much setup, may end up becoming an expensive waste of money.
"The most important thing is that it’s quick and easy to set up, easy to grab and therefore more likely to be used," he said. "The more setup it requires, the less likely you will to be use it."
Before buying a piece of home gym equipment, Zemer recommends considering how much space it requires, how many exercises it supports and whether it will be easy to use consistently. (Jacob Zemer)

Zemer learned that lesson after buying lever arms, attachments that connect to a power rack and move up and down for exercises such as presses, rows and squats. Because the equipment was cumbersome to move, he eventually sold it secondhand.
"The secondhand market of gym equipment is brutal, so if you buy something, and you don't use it, the resale value is next to none," Zemer cautioned.

He recommends prioritizing items that serve multiple purposes, rather than devices designed to target just one body part.
"I always look for equipment that can do multiple things," he said.
"A lot of people think building a home gym requires an elaborate setup, and it doesn't."
Do you need cardio equipment?
Cardio equipment is not essential for everyone, according to the trainer, especially for those who are mobile.
Many people can also raise their heart rate through activities such as walking, running or strength-training workouts performed at a faster pace, he said.

For those who prefer a cardio machine, Zemer recommends choosing an option that is versatile and less likely to aggravate the knees or back, such as a stationary bike or ski erg (an indoor exercise machine that simulates the motion of cross-country skiing).

title: Dementia risk more than quadruples among adults with common disorder
summary: Adults with ADHD had more than four times the risk of dementia or mild cognitive impairment, a University of Pittsburgh study of 187,000 people found.
story: Dr. Elizabeth Landsverk, a geriatric medicine and dementia expert, noted that people with ADHD can have more difficulty with organization, which could be one factor contributing to the higher risk of cognitive impairment.
A common neurodevelopmental disorder could be linked to dementia risk, a new study suggests.

Research led by the University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine, involving more than 187,000 adults aged 50 and older, found that ADHD (attention deficit hyperactivity disorder) was associated with a substantially increased risk of dementia or mild cognitive impairment (MCI).
The observational study looked at electronic health records and genetic information of participants who were enrolled in the U.S. National Institutes of Health All of Us Research Program.
7 NEW DEMENTIA RISK FACTORS REVEALED — INCLUDING ONE MILLIONS STRUGGLE WITH
Cognitive impairment was observed in 6.7% of participants with ADHD versus 3.4% without the disorder — nearly twice the rate.
After researchers adjusted for age, gender and other health conditions, those with ADHD had more than four times the risk.
A common neurodevelopmental disorder could be linked to dementia risk, a new study suggests. (iStock)
The findings — which were published Oct. 7 in JAMA Psychiatry — only show an association and cannot determine that ADHD increases dementia risk, the researchers acknowledged.

"This doesn’t prove that ADHD causes dementia, but seeing the same pattern show up independently in medical records and in people’s genes gives us greater confidence that the association is not simply an artifact of how ADHD gets diagnosed," said senior author Tharick A. Pascoal, associate professor of psychiatry and of neurology at Pitt, in a press release.
"Two different kinds of evidence are pointing in the same direction."
3 THINGS TO AVOID IN MIDDLE AGE COULD MEAN 13 MORE YEARS WITHOUT DEMENTIA, STUDY FINDS
Meanwhile, those with the highest genetic susceptibility to ADHD were found to have a 35% greater risk of dementia than those with the lowest susceptibility.

"Analyzing genetic information alongside years of health records allows us to identify patterns that might not be visible in a smaller or more traditional study," said Guilherme Bauer-Negrini, co-first author and postdoctoral associate in biomedical data science at Pitt, in the release.
"It goes back to nature versus nurture — particularly if we're starting at age 50, as opposed to starting at 20."
"With this kind of data, we can start to investigate what may be driving this association and whether any of those factors could be modified to support healthier cognitive aging."
Understanding the link

Dr. Elizabeth Landsverk, a geriatric medicine and dementia expert with over 20 years of experience treating patients with Alzheimer’s and cognitive decline, noted that people with ADHD can have more difficulty with organization, which could contribute to the higher risk of cognitive impairment, although neurological differences may also play a role.

"It might [be] that keeping on top of health issues and getting to the doctor is more difficult for them," Landsverk, a California-based doctor who is not involved in the study, told Fox News Digital.
Cognitive impairment was observed in 6.7% of participants with ADHD versus 3.4% without the disorder — nearly twice the rate. (iStock)
The study also found that people with ADHD had a 20% higher incidence of utilizing health resources, she pointed out.

"Having just signed up for Medicare, I know that it's really complicated — if you have trouble with focusing and getting things done, you may not be able to get the resources that you need," Landsverk said. "You may not be able to go to the doctor. You may not get your blood pressure taken care of. So there's probably a correlation."
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
"It goes back to nature versus nurture — particularly if we're starting at age 50, as opposed to starting at 20."
ADHD vs dementia
It can be challenging to distinguish between ADHD and cognitive decline, as some of the symptoms may overlap, according to Landsverk.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
"I imagine it can look similar," she said. "You know, you don't remember why you went into a room. You don't know where your keys are, you don't remember the name of an actress."
It is cause for concern if the individual struggles to take care of day-to-day tasks, the expert noted.
The findings only show an association and cannot determine that ADHD increases dementia risk, the researchers acknowledged. (Getty Images)

"You can't pay your bills, you can't get your medications right, you can't get to your appointments, you tell people that you're going to do stuff and then you don't — that's when you need to get checked."
Changes in judgment, mood or social behavior may be more suggestive of dementia than ADHD, Landsverk noted.
Reducing the risk
Although the study found an association between ADHD and cognitive impairment, Landsverk emphasized that some lifestyle behaviors can help people reduce their overall dementia risk.

She pointed to maintaining a healthy weight, avoiding smoking and excessive alcohol, and staying physically active as important modifiable factors, along with controlling blood pressure, cholesterol and diabetes.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
"There's a lot we can do," Landsverk said, recommending a largely plant-based diet and at least 30 minutes of daily exercise.
Physical activity can also help improve mood and focus, she added.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Anyone experiencing persistent problems with memory, focus, organization or managing everyday tasks should consider seeing an expert for an evaluation, Landsverk advised.
