Alongside our engagement with the Committee over the past year, we’ve made the largest safety advancements in Match Group’s history,” Roth wrote in a statement. “Trust and Safety is a foundational priority, and we intend to continue leading the industry in building tools that promote authentic, safe connections.”

Much of that safety work, including the face checks, was already underway before the committee’s investigation, according to Match Group. It reports having seen a roughly 60% reduction in exposure to bad actors in every market since the face checks began.
Hassan similarly said those measures have “already been successful in dramatically reducing the number of matches that their customers have with a scammer.”

“They need to do more, though, because there are still gaps in their systems,” she added. “And they are going to need to stay vigilant in new ways, because the criminals are always changing their technology and their tactics, too.”

title: Kimberly Guilfoyle, U.S. ambassador to Greece, resigns amid misconduct allegations
summary: Guilfoyle, a former Fox News personality, was a top Trump campaign surrogate.
story: U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle, once a top campaign surrogate for President Donald Trump, has resigned at the behest of the White House amid a misconduct probe.
“Serving as the United States Ambassador to Greece has been the honor of a lifetime,” Guilfoyle said Tuesday in a post on X announcing her resignation.
She also addressed “recent allegations against me,” writing, “These allegations are false, and I intend to vigorously defend my name, my reputation, and my integrity.”
Guilfoyle’s post came shortly after new White House press secretary Katie Zacharia told reporters that Guilfoyle had been asked to step down.
“We have asked Ambassador Guilfoyle to resign,” Zacharia said at her inaugural White House press briefing. “She has been a wonderful asset to the team, and we wish her well.”
Speaking to reporters later Tuesday morning, Trump said of Guilfoyle: “She went to Greece. She was doing a good job, but we didn’t like what we were reading.”
He added that he had not spoken to her.

Guilfoyle, 57, the former fiancée of Donald Trump Jr., has been under investigation by the State Department’s inspector general’s office, two people familiar with the decision confirmed to NBC News last week.

The probe came after The Wall Street Journal reported allegations of misconduct in her role as ambassador, including allegations that she bragged about her connections to Greek tycoons who she said funded luxury trips for her. The article cited people who heard the conversation and an audio recording. NBC News has not independently confirmed the allegations.

A Trump donor named Eric Deters came forward this month accusing her of asking him to pay her outstanding $100,000 American Express bill in the days before her 2025 Senate confirmation hearing in exchange for access to senior administration officials.
“She was so desperate for that $100,000. It was a quid pro quo,” Deters told NBC News in an interview.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
“She said I could ask her for anything and everything in Trump world. There was no request too big,” he added.

A text message provided by Deters appeared to show Guilfoyle instructing him to wire the money directly to American Express because “it won’t show up anywhere” that way. He said he did not pay her the money.
Attorneys for Guilfoyle said in a statement Monday that Deters owed her the money for speaking engagements, which he denies.

The attorneys, David Schwartz and Jesse Binnall, also denied allegations of any impropriety involving her travel, saying she “sought, obtained and followed State Department guidance and followed the Department’s travel regulations.”
Asked Tuesday whether she would launch her own investigation into Guilfoyle’s conduct, the U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia, Jeanine Pirro, referred back to the State Department probe.
“I think right now that there is an inspector general investigation in the Department of State. We’ll probably wait to see what comes, what happens with that,” Pirro told reporters.

After the reports about her conduct first surfaced last week, Guilfoyle thought she could save her job and was making calls to allies as recently as Monday in a continued effort to do that, according to a source familiar with the matter.

The person added that there was concern among senior White House aides about what a State Department inspector general probe would find and reveal that has not been made public yet and that could be embarrassing for the president and his administration.
Asked Friday about the reports of Guilfoyle’s conduct, Trump said it was “too bad.”
“I just heard a little bit about it. I don’t know too much, but she was always very nice,” he said.
His tone had hardened by Monday. Asked whether he was considering firing her, he said: “We’re looking at it. We’re not happy.”
Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended Guilfoyle last week.
Vance said “these are accusations” and “we don’t try people in the court of public opinion.”
“Let’s actually see what the facts are. Let’s see what the truth is, and obviously if there was something bad that happened, then people have to suffer consequences for it,” he said.
Rubio, meanwhile, ripped a reporter for asking about the allegations while he was with her in Athens.

“We don’t conduct these things in a press conference on a tarmac in a foreign country because you wrote a story or somebody else wrote a story because some source gave it to you,” Rubio said Thursday.
“I don’t even know if what you’re reporting is true.”

title: Supreme Court to weigh if Nigerian who cooked for terrorists can be denied asylum
summary: The Supreme Court agreed to consider the Trump administration’s bid to deny asylum to a man officials say provided material support to terrorists in Nigeria by cooking food for them.
story: WASHINGTON — The Supreme Court on Tuesday agreed to consider the Trump administration’s bid to deny asylum to a man officials say provided material support to terrorists in Nigeria by cooking food for them.

The case involving Izuchukwu Ozurumba focuses on a provision of immigration law that bars anyone from entering the U.S. if they have “engaged in terrorist activity,” which includes providing material support.
The Trump administration has cracked down on asylum claims as part of its broader anti-immigration policy.

Ozurumba claims he took the job working as a camp cook in 2022 before finding out that it was run by a separatist group called the Unknown Gunmen. He worked there for about six months, half of which was unpaid, before escaping, he said.

Aimee Mayer-Salins, a lawyer with the nonprofit Amica Center for Immigrant Rights who represents Ozurumba, said the Trump administration’s broad interpretation of the law would make it “very hard for people fleeing persecution to seek safety in the United States.”
Even “the most insignificant” alleged support for a militant group would be enough to deny them entry under the government’s interpretation, she added.
Ozurumba sought asylum in the U.S. after crossing the southern border in July 2023, claiming members of the Unknown Gunmen had threatened to kill him.
For Subscribers
An immigration judge initially rejected his asylum claim, finding that Ozurumba had provided material support to the group by cooking three meals a day.
For Subscribers

Ozurumba was subsequently deported in April 2025, but his case continued, and five months later the Richmond, Virginia-based 4th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled in his favor, saying that cooking did not qualify as material support.
Mayer-Salins declined to say where Ozurumba is now, noting only that he is in hiding.
The justices will hear arguments and issue a ruling later in the court term, which runs until June.
In the coming weeks, they will also decide whether to hear the Trump administration’s appeal seeking to maintain a broad block on asylum claims at the U.S.-Mexico border.

title: Supreme Court to hear Trump attempt to withhold DOGE documents
summary: The Supreme Court allowed a watchdog group to seek further information about the internal operations of the Trump administration’s Department of Government Efficiency that played a key role in firing thousands of federal workers and canceling various streams of government funding.
story: WASHINGTON — The Supreme Court on Tuesday took up the Trump administration’s bid to prevent a watchdog group from seeking information about the Department of Government Efficiency, which played a key role in firing thousands of federal workers and canceling government funding.
The court agreed to hear a Justice Department appeal that sought to prevent Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington from obtaining the records.
The underlying litigation focuses on whether DOGE is an agency that is subject to the Freedom of Information Act. A ruling is due by the end of June.
The Trump administration has argued that DOGE, spearheaded by former administration adviser Elon Musk, was not subject to what are known as FOIA requests.
Nikhel Sus, a lawyer at CREW, said in a statement that lower courts had uniformly ruled against DOGE.
“We will continue to pursue transparency for the American people, who deserve to know the details of the Trump administration’s efforts to unilaterally remake the federal government,” he added.
The White House did not immediately respond to a request seeking comment.
For Subscribers

DOGE, which played a key role in dismantling the U.S. Agency for International Development, was a controversial feature of Trump’s early months in office, triggering various lawsuits. Its operations have since dwindled.

The case had already reached the Supreme Court once at an earlier stage of the litigation. Then, in a provisional decision, the court blocked parts of a lower court ruling that required thousands of pages of information to be handed over.
It also meant that plaintiffs’ lawyers could not depose Amy Gleason, the DOGE administrator.

Litigation has since continued. As a result of the Supreme Court’s earlier intervention, the plaintiffs narrowed their requests for information, but the government still objected. After losing in lower courts, Solicitor General D. John Sauer again asked the justices to weigh in.
For Subscribers
The information requests remained on hold while the case plays out.

The plaintiffs say the information they still want is about DOGE guidance to its workers on the canceling of contracts and firing of government workers. None of those requests concern any communications with the White House that may be off-limits under FOIA, they say.
A key question lurking in the case is whether DOGE is technically a government agency and therefore subject to FOIA, which allows members of the public to seek internal documents.
The Trump administration says that, despite its name, DOGE is merely a presidential advisory body that is not subject to public records requests under FOIA.

Further complicating matters, when DOGE was set up, it effectively took the place of a previous government entity called the U.S. Digital Service. The Trump administration now refers to the body as the U.S. DOGE Service, or USDS.
Soon after Trump took office in January 2025, CREW filed a FOIA request seeking information about DOGE. The group later filed suit.

In March 2025, U.S. District Court Judge Christopher Cooper in Washington ruled DOGE is “likely” covered by FOIA, saying that “the public would be irreparably harmed by an indefinite delay in unearthing the records CREW seeks.”
The documents in question all relate back to the question of whether DOGE is a government agency.

title: Jenna and Sheinelle Weigh In on Shane Gillis’ ‘SNL’ Monologue About Women’s Gym Clothes: ‘It Feels Mean’
summary: Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones gave their take on Shane Gillis calling women “whores” in his monologue while hosting “Saturday Night Live.”
story: Jenna Bush Hager and Sheinelle Jones are speaking out about the controversy that followed after Shane Gillis called women “whores” in his monologue while hosting “Saturday Night Live” on Oct. 10.

“I haven’t been to the gym in so long. I didn’t know women just dressed like whores now,” he said. “Look, I’m sorry. There’s no other way to describe — have you seen it? I’ve seen it. The shorts. Have you seen the shorts?”

Jenna and Sheinelle discussed how people were infuriated, noting that a lot of men chastised Gillis for his choice of words. Sheinelle then said she tends to give more rope when comedy is involved, but he may have pushed the envelope too much with his language.

“With comedy, I am a bit more, I guess, lenient because I do believe there is room for comedians to be able to push the button, and not have to feel like, ‘Oh, am I going to get canceled or this or that?’” she said.

“My challenge is the word ‘whore.’ Look, I have girlfriends who I know exactly what shorts he’s talking about, and they’re like, ‘Sheinelle, you need to wear these,’ and it’s exactly what he’s saying. It’s like ruching. Your butt looks bigger. You know, all the things. And I know why they’re wearing them. So, whatever. If that’s what they want to wear, Godspeed. But I think when you say the word whore, I think it feels almost derogatory.”
“Not almost,” Jenna said.
“It just feels condescending,” Sheinelle continued.
“I wouldn’t want my kids to listen to that,” Jenna said.
“It feels mean,” Sheinelle said. “And that is the energy that I think made people upset.”
Sheinelle also felt there was a sense of hypocrisy in what Gillis said when she pointed out that men go shirtless at the gym and “are proud of their bodies.”
“So if the guy can be proud of his body, let the girl be proud of her body,” she said.
Jenna also took issue with Gillis amplifying his thoughts, which speaks to a larger problem.

“Who is he to comment on women’s bodies?” she said. “And I think we’ve become this culture, Shane Gillis among many, where online creators — I mean, he’s obviously on ‘Saturday Night Live,’ but this perpetuates what is happening in our culture where people are commenting on women’s looks.”
Sheinelle said that has almost made it acceptable to do so, prompting Jenna to say it’s not OK.
“If we want to be good role models for our children, stop talking about the way women look. Period,” Jenna said.

“And I think you know, there’s many of women have said, ‘This is enough.’ And, so, I think, honestly, and especially in the time we’re living in, I wouldn’t want my son to hear that. If my husband talked like that about somebody — he would never. But if he did, I would be disgusted by it.”
Jenna also said it’s important for her to remember her children are watching, especially when trying to navigate difficult subjects.

“I think when we’re having conversations in here around horrible things that are happening in the world and how to talk to our kids about it, maybe the first place to start is for some of these people to start acting like role models,” she said.

“So for me, I’m like, ‘OK,’ if I’m trying to be open with comedy, then it’s ‘OK.’ You know, you’re going to poke fun at the girl. You can poke fun at the guy without a shirt on. You didn’t go to him, but you could have,” Sheinelle said. “But just the energy of the word ‘whore.’ I mean, that’s what gets me.”
Jenna also pointed out that there’s a larger problem in the world revolving around mocking how women look.

“We have a culture where there’s casual cruelty about the way people look, constantly. And imagine if you heard your daughter talking about the way that some of these people online talk about women. It’s not OK.”

title: What to Know About ‘Breaking Bad’ Actor RJ Mitte’s Cause of Death and Cerebral Palsy Diagnosis
summary: RJ Mitte, “Breaking Bad” actor, died of suicide, his representatives said about his cause of death. What the actor said about living with cerebral palsy.
story: RJ Mitte was one of the emotional centers of “Breaking Bad,” playing a teenager with cerebral palsy, a condition he lived with in real life since he was a toddler.
The actor passed away at 34.

Bryan Cranston, who played his father on the hit TV show, wrote in an Instagram post that he was in “deep despair.” He recalled Mitte was 14 when he was cast as his son, a role “he played with joy and enthusiasm.”
“Born with Cerebral Palsy, he never — ever — allowed that challenge to be an excuse for anything. He met the demanding shooting schedule head on with great determination,” Cranston wrote.
RJ Mitte’s Cause of Death
Mitte died on Monday, Oct. 12, in Brownsville, Texas, where he had moved, the local Justice of the Peace Judge Cyndi Hinojosa told NBC News.
“Sadly, we can confirm that suicide was the cause of death,” Sean Reilly, his representative, said in a statement to NBC News on Tuesday, Oct. 13.
“It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate RJ Mitte,” his reps previously said.
Mitte lived with cerebral palsy and drew from his own experience to bring authenticity to his “Breaking Bad” role and build “a platform on disability awareness and inclusion,” they added.
What RJ Mitte Said About His Cerebral Palsy
The actor was diagnosed with cerebral palsy at around 3 years old, and underwent physical, occupational and speech therapy, he told Vice in 2016.

Mitte was a severe toe walker so part of the treatment involved doctors bending his foot as far as it would go and putting it in a cast, “which was not fun,” he recalled. A few weeks later, the cast would be taken off, his foot bent even further and immobilized in a cast again — a process that was repeated until his foot was flat.
“I’m always working at taking control. It’s a fight. It will always be a fight,” he said about his body.

“Breaking Bad” showed real characters that everyone could relate to, Mitte noted. He played the son of Walter White — a high school chemistry teacher who starts making and selling crystal meth as a way to secretly make more money for his family after he’s diagnosed with terminal cancer.
Mitte’s teenage character was based on a real person with cerebral palsy who was friends with the show’s creator, Mitte said on The Joe Vulpis Podcast a week before his death.
The actor kept the forearm crutches his character used in “Breaking Bad.” That was the only thing he “truly wanted” from the set, Mitte said, though he didn’t use them in real life.
The actor was reluctant to become an advocate at first, but found himself naturally doing advocacy work. He created an anti-bullying campaign and took part in philanthropic work.
“I’m lucky that I can be an advocate, I’m lucky that I can do what I do. … I think we all have an obligation to have an impact for the positive,” he said.
Asked how people with disabilities can remove the stigma of not being able-bodied, Mitte urged others to be open.

“Don’t hide your disability. Don’t hide whatever it is that you’re hiding — and I’m not just talking about a physical disability, I’m talking about a mental disability. Show who you are and what you are to the world,” he said.
In 2025, the actor got engaged to his longtime girlfriend after he proposed during a fundraising gala for United Cerebral Palsy (UCP) of San Diego, People reported. He was an ambassador for UCP.
“I’m thrilled to have found my person, my partner in life who makes me want to be better, no matter what we’re doing,” he said about his engagement.
What Is Cerebral Palsy?

It’s a group of neurologic disorders caused when a baby’s brain is damaged, usually as it develops in the womb, disrupting a child’s ability to control muscles and movement, and maintain posture and balance, according to the National Library of Medicine.
While most people with cerebral palsy have the condition at birth, it may not be diagnosed until months or years later, the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke explains.
Symptoms depend on how the condition affects the body — it can cause arm or leg weakness, stiff muscles, involuntary movements and other problems.
There are many different types and levels of disability, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
“A person with severe CP might need to use special equipment to be able to walk or might not be able to walk at all and might need lifelong care,” the CDC notes.
“A person with mild CP, on the other hand, might walk a little awkwardly, but might not need any special help.”
Mitte had mild cerebral palsy and stopped wearing leg braces at 13, he told L.A. Parent. But his character in “Breaking Bad” used forearm crutches.
There’s no cure for cerebral palsy, but treatment such as physical therapy, medication, surgery and mobility devices can help people manage their symptoms.

title: Lindsay Czarniak Makes the Case for Why Husband Craig Melvin Should Win ‘Sexiest Man’ Contest
summary: There is no mystery about who Lindsay Czarniak will be voting for in People’s Sexiest Man Alive Readers’ Choice poll: her husband, Craig Melvin.
story: There is no mystery about who Emmy-winning broadcaster Lindsay Czarniak will be voting for in People’s Sexiest Man Alive Readers’ Choice poll: her husband, Craig Melvin.

The TODAY co-anchor is among the nominees featured in the “hotter than your cup of coffee in the morning” category for morning show personalities, going up against Michael Strahan, Gio Benitez and Vladimir Duthiers.
And Lindsay isn’t shy about urging people to support her piping hot husband.
“Here’s what: I just think he should win,” she said in an Instagram reel while appropriately holding a cup of coffee.
“I think as a wife, and also as a journalist, I’m uniquely qualified to weigh in,” she said on the video posted on October 12.

“He is an amazing dad, tremendous husband, teammate, partner, always so supportive and encouraging,” she said. “He makes a mean chili ... he is a pro at candle-making. He is really good at debating. This is true — and I mean in the most positive of ways.
“But beyond that, he is someone who really cares about where he’s from, leaves people feeling really good about themselves in his presence,” she continued.

“And beyond all those things that make him sexy on the outside — like, let’s be honest, the dimple, guys, it’s the dimple — I think it’s his character and his makeup on the inside that make us think that really, you know, he’s the sexiest man alive.”
She ended her video with a call to action for viewers: “I hope you’ll vote, and if you do, I hope you’ll vote Melvin. And he is definitely hotter than my first cup of coffee.”
While voting in the survey is now closed, the results will be available starting Oct. 20.
Of course, Craig’s TODAY co-hosts couldn’t help but poke some fun at him.
“We’ve been campaigning feverishly,” said Carson Daly with a twinkle in his eye.
After they watched a clip from Lindsay’s Instagram video, Craig asked, “How much did you pay for that?”
Savannah Guthrie, Dylan Dreyer, Jenna Bush Hager, Sheinelle Jones and Carson applauded Lindsay’s broadcasting skills and her sincerity.
“She’s the best, man!” said Carson.
“So even if you lose, you’ve won,” Dylan pointed out.
“You’re sweating more right now,” Carson commented.
“I am so hot right now,” said Craig, clearly embarrassed by the attention.
“Yes, you are!” joked Savannah. “That’s the point!”

title: Bryan Cranston Remembers ‘Sweet’ ‘Breaking Bad’ Son RJ Mitte After His Death at 34
summary: Bryan Cranston mourned the death of RJ Mitte, who played his son on “Breaking Bad.”
story: This story discusses suicide. If you or someone you know is in crisis, call or text 988 to reach the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. You can also text HOME to 741741 or visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources for additional resources.
Bryan Cranston is mourning the death of “Breaking Bad” co-star RJ Mitte, who played his son on the hit AMC series.
Representatives for Mitte confirmed Oct. 12 that he had died at age 34. His cause of death was suicide, reps said.
On “Breaking Bad,” Mitte played Walter “Flynn” White Jr., a teen with cerebral palsy and the son of Cranston’s Walter White.
Cranston wrote in an Instagram post on Oct. 12 that he was in “deep despair.” He recalled Mitte was 14 when he was cast as his son, a role “he played with joy and enthusiasm.”

“Born with Cerebral Palsy, he never — ever — allowed that challenge to be an excuse for anything. He met the demanding shooting schedule head on with great determination,” Cranston captioned a photo of the two of them.

“Always listening to the advice that his TV parents (Anna Gunn and myself) gave him — but being a teenager, sometimes mischievously ignoring the counsel in order to learn the hard way… He was one of the stars of a hit TV show — but still a kid,” he added.

Mitte appeared in 56 episodes of “Breaking Bad” between the five seasons it aired from 2008 through 2013, according to IMDB. Cranston wrote that Mitte was hardly a seasoned veteran when they began the series, but he eventually grew into his own.

“That kid was pretty raw when we started shooting the pilot in February of 2007, but little by little we watched him grow into a really fine actor,” he wrote. “He parlayed his experience on the show to be a vocal advocate for performers with disabilities, and was the head of a philanthropic organization with a focus on helping the disabled community.
“All that promise and potential now is such a loss,” he continued. “It is especially devastating to hear that he took his own life. Why?”
Cranston also looked back at how they recently spoke and discussed getting together in person.

“We were texting each other just a few weeks ago — figuring out when we could meet for lunch,” he wrote. “I don’t know if that lunch would have changed his future…But I do know that I loved him, and thoroughly enjoyed being with him throughout the years on the series, and after the spotlight on Breaking Bad dimmed…I’ll miss you, son.”
Reps for Mitte confirmed to NBC News on Oct. 12 that the actor had died.
“It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate RJ Mitte,” a representative said in a statement.

Texas Justice of the Peace Judge Cyndi Hinojosa also confirmed that Mitte died Oct. 12 in Brownsville, Texas, adding he was “very beloved in our community” and that “his family has deep ties” in the city.

In addition to his acting work, Mitte was an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Children’s, as well president of The Mitte Foundation, supporting philanthropic efforts and community initiatives, his reps said. He also used “his platform to challenge stereotypes and promote greater representation for people with disabilities,” the statement added.

title: Teen Vogue, Wattpad to Publish Original Short Stories With Fan Fiction-Style Daily Drops. Read a Preview
summary: Teen Vogue and Wattpad Books will publish Tay Marley’s next romance story in daily installments for free online.
story: It is a truth universally acknowledged that a good story starts with a good first line. In TODAY’s “Cold Open,” authors tease their buzzy upcoming release by revealing and explaining its first line, paragraph or page.
Tay Marley, known for writing the Wattpad romance that inspired the Noah Beck-led movie “Sidelined,” is returning to form with the release of her next story.

“Under the Northern Stars” is a romantic short story about Gemma, a small-town girl obsessed with science, and her neighbor Leo, a bronc-riding champion. The 11,000-word story, created in partnership with Wattpad, will be available on Teen Vogue’s website in daily chapters, hearkening back to the fan fiction convention of publishing in installments.

The first chapter will be available to read for free on TeenVogue.com starting Oct. 19. Each day of that week, a new part will be available to read, with the final chapter dropping Friday, Oct. 23. Readers can sign up for a newsletter on Teen Vogue’s site that will alert them as soon as the next installment is available to read.

“It’s been such an honor to collaborate with Wattpad Books and Teen Vogue to bring you ‘Under the Northern Stars,’ a short story about Gemma and Leo and their romance that takes place under the stars,” Marley tells TODAY.com in a statement. “I absolutely loved writing about these two teens, a shared fence line, and futures pulling them in opposite directions. Are they written in the stars?”
Teen Vogue’s Creative Editorial Director Mi-Anne Chan says the goal of the website’s partnership with Wattpad is to create a new space for fan engagement and community for an original fiction work.

“Under the Northern Stars” is the first of three original pieces of fiction that will publish on Teen Vogue. “Read To Me,” by Ariana Godoy, will follow in February 2027, and a new short story by “After” author Anna Todd with E.M. Wilson will publish in spring 2027. All three stories will also explore Gen Z’s relationship with astrology, with themes of “compatibility, identity, and modern relationships through the archetypes and relationship dynamics associated with the zodiac,” Teen Vogue says in a news release.
The goal is to engage readers not just in the stories, but in the experience of following the serialized fiction format.

“Something that I, as a fan fiction and original fiction reader on the internet, really love about the genre is waiting patiently for the next chapter drop, engaging with the community in the comments and online, and that’s something that I really, really wanted to bring to Teen Vogue,” Chan says.

“Under the Northern Stars” specifically brings the familiar trope of a “small town neighborhood romance,” Chan says, and is “giving debut Taylor’s Version-type energy,” referring to Taylor Swift’s first album, which is celebrating 20 years since its release this October.
Read on for the first two paragraphs of the short story.
Read the Opening Lines of ‘Under the Northern Stars’

Out here, in the vast countryside of Western Montana, most people who want to see their neighbors hop on a four-wheeler and take a two-minute drive down a narrow dirt road. Or maybe you’ll walk for a half hour through the rolling paddocks and then hop a boundary line. On my family’s slice of land, where I’ve got a small cabin out back that I call the lab (with my equipment and a deck where my telescope stands), I’ve got the privilege of being right up beside the neighbor’s pool house. Too close for comfort.

Three of my favorite things in the world are the stars, my family, and this land I grew up on. Three things I don’t love are leaving for college at the end of summer, snakes, and my egocentric, bronc-riding neighbor, Leo. He moved in next door when he was nine and decided to nickname me after the only scientist he knew, Albert. My love for science and perfect-score pop quizzes became fuel for the teasing that went on for years. We’re older now, but the tone was set. Now that school’s done, it’s easier to ignore him.

title: ‘Breaking Bad’ Actor RJ Mitte Dies at 34
summary: Actor RJ Mitte, best known for his role as Walter “Flynn” White Jr., has died, his reps confirmed.
story: RJ Mitte, the actor best known for his role as Walter “Flynn” White Jr. on “Breaking Bad,” has died, his reps confirmed to NBC News on Oct. 12.
“It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights advocate RJ Mitte,” his reps said in a statement.

Texas Justice of the Peace Judge Cyndi Hinojosa also confirmed with NBC News that Mitte died on Monday afternoon in Brownsville, Texas. She said the actor was “very beloved in our community” and that “his family has deep ties” in the city.
Hinojosa added that he “will be very much missed,” adding it’s “rare to have someone not from here devote so much time and effort.”
They did not share a cause of death at this time.

Mitte lived with cerebral palsy and, according to his reps, he drew from his own experience to bring authenticity to his “Breaking Bad” role and build “a platform on disability awareness and inclusion.”
Cerebral palsy affects movement, balance and posture and is caused by damage that occurs to a baby’s brain, most often before birth, according to Mayo Clinic.

“Beyond entertaining friends and family around the world, he served as an ambassador for United Cerebral Palsy and Shriners Children’s. He also served as president of The Mitte Foundation, supporting philanthropic efforts and community initiatives, while using his platform to challenge stereotypes and promote greater representation for people with disabilities,” the statement continued.
His reps asked people to respect his family and close friends’ privacy at this time.

Among his other acting credits include “Switched at Birth,” “The Oak Room,” “The Recall,” “Westhamption” and most recently “Talking to Strangers.” He also had a number of projects in works like “One Eye Open” and “Cassi,” according to IMDB.

title: What’s Going on With Kelly Clarkson, the Brooklyn Store and the Animatronic Bird?
summary: What’s going on with Kelly Clarkson and the Brooklyn store? Here’s a recap of everything that happened.
story: “Catch Me Up” is a TODAY series where our experts and journalists bring readers up to speed on the day’s biggest headlines.
Did Kelly Clarkson have a “Pretty Woman” moment while shopping?
Or was she insisting on buying an item that wasn’t for sale?

The Grammy-winning singer ignited a back-and-forth on social media with the owner of a curiosity store in Brooklyn, New York, with a post on X about what she says was her negative treatment during a visit.
All of it revolves around a $15,000 mechanical bird puppet that mounts on the wall. Yes, you read that correctly.
Here’s what to know about the drama.
Kelly Clarkson Posts That She Was Treated Like Julia Roberts in “Pretty Woman”
The singer posted on X on Oct. 10 that she drove “all the way to Brooklyn” to check out a store she thought “looked really rad.”
Clarkson is also a host on “The Voice” and the former host of “The Kelly Clarkson Show,” both of which aired on NBC. NBC is a division of NBCUniversal, which is also the parent company of TODAY.

Clarkson, 44, wrote that she was contemplating buying a “few things” from the store when someone who worked there “looked at as if I couldn’t afford it and was told he could find something comparable for me.”
“Wow, dude. You’re an idiot and just lost a huge sale,” she wrote.

She finished by comparing her experience to a scene from the movie “Pretty Woman.” Vivian Ward, played by Julia Roberts, is dismissed by a condescending saleswoman while shopping at a Beverly Hills boutique because she is dressed casually.
“But y’all should go check out Art of Play in Brooklyn if you enjoy being treated like Julia Roberts character in Pretty Woman,” Clarkson wrote.
The Business Says Clarkson’s Claims Involved Molly, an Animatronic Bird
The owner of Art of Play aimed to clarify the situation in an Instagram post on Oct. 11.

“Yesterday, Kelly Clarkson visited us in Brooklyn and inquired about buying ‘Molly,’ a one-of-a-kind singing and dancing bird automaton who plays an important role in the magic shows we host here,” the company wrote. “Molly is permanently attached to the wall and isn’t for sale. However, the negative experience Kelly described on twitter would resonate with anyone who has ever felt judged in a shop.”
Art of Play added that anyone looking to make a purchase or look around is “equally welcome” at the store.

“Imagine our surprise when our small local business was suddenly attacked by 8 million people who have never visited our store,” the statement continued. “It’s been a surreal experience to be the focus of such widespread outrage after just one mention by a celebrity.”
Art of Play then tried to make light of the situation by name-checking one of Clarkson’s biggest hits, “Stronger (What Doesn’t Kill You).”

“Thanks to all our friends for their support and welcome to all the curious folks who have discovered us amidst the drama. We’re going to keep our heads down and hopefully, we can clear things up with Kelly someday. As a talented popular singer once said ‘what doesn’t kill you makes you stronger.’”
What to Know About Molly, the $15,000 Animatronic Bird
The shop posted about Molly on Instagram in February 2025, calling the elaborate mechanical puppet the store’s “mascot.”
It was created by Seattle-based artist Bliss Kolb, who lists the bird on his website, but does not have a price on it. Kolb did not immediately respond to request for comment by TODAY.com.

“When you turn her crank Molly begins to sing and dance and move to and fro, just like a real bird,” Art of Play wrote. “The illusion is uncanny and we have come to develop a real affection for Molly.”
The shop wrote that Bliss came to New York in 2025 to fix the bird.

“Now, Molly is singing and dancing better than ever. However, she remains very delicate and very expensive so Molly is one of the few items in the shop that has a “Do Not Touch” sign,” the store wrote.
Art of Play Says Kelly Clarkson Spent ‘5 Minutes’ in the Store
In a follow-up post on Instagram on Oct. 11, Art of Play said that Kolb, the creator of Molly the animatronic bird, was willing to sell Clarkson a matching one for $15,000.

“During the 5 minutes she spent in the store, she inquired about our mechanical bird puppet named Molly,” the store wrote. “We explained that while Molly is permanently attached to the wall and serves as a de facto mascot for our shop, a nearly identical automaton is owned by the creator of the machines, a brilliant artist named Bliss Kolb who lives in Seattle. He told us he would be willing to part with Molly’s twin for $15,000. We explained all of this to Kelly Clarkson.”
The post said Clarkson was also presented with another option.

“We also offered to show her a different singing bird automaton, made by a traditional clockmaking shop in Germany, that she could have taken home with her that day. It costs about $2,000. She did not stick around long enough to see it,” the store wrote.
The store added that it has reached out to Clarkson to “clear the air.”
“We really do wish her the best and hope that someday we can all laugh about this misunderstanding.”
Clarkson Says She Was Told The Bird Was For Sale
Clarkson fired back on Art of Play’s claim that Molly was not for sale in a post on X on Oct. 11, claiming the store changed its tune since she’s been gone.

“Cool, cool. Sure, it wasn’t for sale. That’s the narrative Art of Play is gonna go with 👍 so the whole conversation we had when I asked you if it was for sale whilst pointing to the price tag hanging on the wall with the title Singing Bird didn’t happen as you elevator eyed me saying in a condescending tone ‘yes, it’s for sale but it costs 15,000 dollars so if you’d like me to find something comparable for you I can,’” Clarkson wrote. “That all never happened and now it’s not for sale. Okay, cool. So you’re not only rude, you’re also a liar. Got it ✅”

Clarkson wrote that she “obviously” supports small businesses because she was visiting one, “but you don’t get a free pass to treat people less than in your store just because you are a small business.”
The singer maintained her position about how she was treated.
“It’s not that hard to be kind,” she wrote. “I never blast people but you my friend were an exception. Your store is really cool. Unfortunately, you aren’t.”
Clarkson attached a photo of Molly with what appears to be a price tag on it, but it’s unclear if that was taken by her or if it’s an older photo that was online.
How Have People Reacted to the Situation?
Some commenters on Art of Play’s initial Oct. 11 Instagram post said they had been to the store and seen a pricetag on Molly the bird, refuting the store’s claim that it wasn’t for sale.
Others claimed to have encountered similarly difficult behavior.
“You have such a greatly curated shop but the several times I’ve been in I’m met with rude or obnoxious behavior by your staff to us or to other customers,” a commenter wrote.
“The fact that other customers had wonderful experiences at your store does not mean Kelly Clarkson couldn’t have had a terrible one. Both can be true at the same time,” another wrote.
“You can just tell from their response how they’re just rude and horrible people,” a commenter wrote on Clarkson’s post on X.
Others were critical of Clarkson.

“I don’t know either parties, but I think it’s wild that a big, mega-rich celebrity would put a small business on blast, knowing that threatening harassment would ensue from fans,” one Instagram commenter wrote. “Celebrities don’t know what it’s like to be told no. Just move on with your day!”

“Please God, never let me get to the level of tone deaf where I’m publicly whining about a stupid $15k TOY bird that 99% of Americans could never afford b/c they are struggling to make ends meet,” one commenter wrote on X.
Art of Play’s Yelp page has been flooded with 1-star and 5-star reviews since the drama bubbled over, with people taking sides in support of Clarkson or the store.

title: Shane Gillis Faces Backlash for ‘SNL’ Monologue Joke About Women’s Gym Attire
summary: Standup comedian Shane Gillis has come under fire for delivering what many people are calling a misogynistic monologue when he hosted “Saturday Night Live.”
story: Standup comedian Shane Gillis has come under fire for delivering what many people are calling a misogynistic joke about the way women dress at the gym during his “Saturday Night Live” monologue.
Gillis, who hosted the Oct. 10 episode of the sketch comedy show, began the bit by explaining how difficult it is for him to work out at a health club.

“Going to the public gym as a fat guy, especially in New York, is a nightmare, dude. It’s just the hottest gay guys you’ve ever seen. They’re jacked, and they look at me like, ‘Yeah, right.’ I know, dude,” he began.

“Also, I haven’t been to the gym in so long. I didn’t know women just dressed like whores now,” he continued. “Look, I’m sorry. There’s no other way to describe — have you seen it? I’ve seen it. The shorts. Have you seen the shorts?
Social media lit up with people blasting Gillis.
“Women wearing shorts at the gym does not make them whores. It makes the men calling them whores misogynists,” Emmy-winning “Schitt’s Creek” star Dan Levy said in an Instagram reel.
“I’m speechless that something like that can exist on live national television,” he added.
Comedian Phoebe Robinson posted a video of herself reacting to the joke.
“Women are dressed like whores? What is the joke?” she said in part.
BuzzFeed Editorial Director Spencer Althouse described the monologue on X as “very awkward,” while another viewer wrote, “This is so disgusting.”

“I don’t know what turns my stomach more, the fact that Shane Gillis was on Saturday Night Live tonight and said women at the gym ‘dress like whores’ or that there was people in that audience who found his disgusting bit of so-called humor funny,” someone else wrote on X.
“have you at any point considered that women are tired of being called ‘whores’ for existing in public,” another user replied to someone on X who said the monologue was “funny.”
Feminist writer Jessica Valenti also posted a TikTok video about the joke in the context of the investigation into a rape allegation at Cornell University, captioning it, “I am LIVID.”
“Shane Gillis knows that there is a major national conversation happening right now about sexual assault,” Valenti said in part.
“And so I don’t want to hear a single f------ word about how this was just in bad taste, this was a mistake, he didn’t realize, it was just tone deaf. No,” Valenti added.
TODAY.com has reached out to representatives for “Saturday Night Live” and Gillis for comment but did not immediately hear back.
In his monologue, Gillis also faced backlash for jokes referring to his older siblings as his “two big fat b---- sisters” and comparing his hairline to Hitler’s.

Gillis’ comedy career has boomed in recent years. In July, he set a Guinness World Record for most tickets sold for a comedy show by a solo comedian. He starred in the comedy series “Tires” and headlined his own comedy special, “Beautiful Dogs,” both on Netflix. He has also appeared in multiple Bud Light commercials.

Gillis has courted controversy with “SNL” before. In 2019, he was fired from the show days after it was announced that he was joining the cast due to resurfaced clips of Gillis using racist slurs and making homophobic jokes on a podcast. Despite his firing, he went on to host “SNL” in 2024 and 2025.
“Most of you probably have no idea who I am … I was fired from this show,” Gillis said in his 2024 “SNL” monologue. “A while ago. But, you know. Don’t look that up, please.”

title: Store Responds After Kelly Clarkson Says Staff Treated Her Like Julia Roberts’ ‘Pretty Woman’ Character
summary: Brooklyn specialty shop Art of Play has responded after singer Kelly Clarkson accused the store of treating her “like Julia Roberts character in Pretty Woman.”
story: Brooklyn specialty shop Art of Play has responded after singer Kelly Clarkson accused the store of treating her “like Julia Roberts character in Pretty Woman.”
Art of Play posted a statement on its Instagram page after Clarkson tweeted on Oct. 10 that she visited the store, with her eye on a few items but instead was “looked at as if I couldn’t afford it.”
Clarkson added that she “was told he could find something comparable for me.”
“Wow, dude. You’re an idiot and just lost a huge sale,” Clarkson wrote on X, before naming the New York City store.
The small business responded on Oct. 11, saying in a statement that Clarkson had attempted to buy a permanent installation that is not for sale.

However, the negative experience Kelly described on twitter would resonate with anyone who has ever felt judged in a shop.”
The store, which wrote that it had become the subject of backlash after Clarkson’s post, thanked those who supported it.

“Thanks to all our friends for their support and welcome to all the curious folks who have discovered us amidst the drama,” Art of Play wrote in the statement, before referencing Clarkson’s hit song. “We’re going to keep our heads down and hopefully, we can clear things up with Kelly someday. As a talented popular singer once said ‘what doesn’t kill you makes you stronger.’”

Clarkson did not immediately respond to TODAY.com’s request for comment. But in another post on X, Clarkson challenged the store’s statement, describing the staff as “not only rude, you’re also a liar.”
“Cool, cool. Sure, it wasn’t for sale. That’s the narrative Art of Play is gonna go with 👍” Clarkson wrote on the social media platform Oct. 11.
The singer then continued with her version of events.

“So the whole conversation we had when I asked you if it was for sale whilst pointing to the price tag hanging on the wall with the title Singing Bird didn’t happen as you elevator eyed me saying in a condescending tone ‘yes, it’s for sale but it costs 15,000 dollars so if you’d like me to find something comparable for you I can.’” she wrote in the post, appearing to convey sarcasm. “That all never happened and now it’s not for sale.”
The singer also hit back at criticisms that she doesn’t support small businesses.

“You don’t get a free pass to treat people less than in your store just because you are a small business,” she wrote. “It’s not that hard to be kind. I never blast people but you my friend were an exception.”
She concluded by saying, “Your store is really cool.”
“Unfortunately, you aren’t,” she wrote.

Art of Play did not immediately respond to TODAY.com’s request for comment on Clarkson’s Oct. 11 post. The store, however, shared a follow-up post to its Instagram early Oct. 12 in an effort to “clarify one additional detail about Kelly Clarkson’s visit.”

“During the 5 minutes she spent in the store, she inquired about our mechanical bird puppet named Molly,” the Oct. 12 post from Art of Play said. “We explained that while Molly is permanently attached to the wall and serves as a de facto mascot for our shop, a nearly identical automaton is owned by the creator of the machines, a brilliant artist named Bliss Kolb who lives in Seattle. He told us he would be willing to part with Molly’s twin for $15,000.”
The store said employees offered to show her another option for a singing bird that was available to take home that day for $2,000 but Clarkson “did not stick around long enough to see it.”
Art of Play said it reached out to the singer directly to “clear the air.”
Art of Play, which sits in the neighborhood of Brooklyn Heights, is a specialty store that features home goods in addition to magic-themed gifts, cards and games.

In her post, Clarkson said that she “drove all the way to Brooklyn” to take a peek at the store, already with a few things in mind to purchase. She compared her experience to that of Julia Roberts’ “Pretty Woman” character Vivian Ward when she is brushed off by a Beverly Hills salesperson who assumes she can’t afford the expensive items in the store because of her casual appearance.
Art of Play said in the statement that the store invites all shoppers to play with their items.
“And they do, many stay for hours enjoying our puzzles, games and toys,” the store said.
The criticisms they’ve been receiving have taken them by surprise, the store said in the statement.

“Imagine our surprise when our small local business was suddenly attacked by 8 million people who have never visited our store,” the statement said. “It’s been a surreal experience to be the focus of such widespread outrage after just one mention by a celebrity.”

The bird automaton appears to have not been available for purchase in the past. Several weeks ago, the store had made a post about their “favorite items not for sale,” featuring an image of the bird automaton.

Since the parties’ comments, the internet has been divided with Clarkson’s fans flocking to the store’s pages to express their disappointment. Many others, including New York locals, have been commenting as well, sharing their positive experiences with the shop.

title: Ashley Padilla is a Mom Trying To Hold it Together After Babysitter Canceled on ‘SNL’
summary: Ashley Padilla joined the Weekend Update segment of “Saturday Night Live” as a frazzled mom whose babysitter canceled.
story: It’s hard to keep it together when you’ve had it up to here!

Ashley Padilla joined the Weekend Update segment of “Saturday Night Live” as a frazzled mom whose babysitter canceled. Given the circumstances, problem child Coco, played by new cast member Grace Reiter, had to tag along as well.
While the mom tried really, really hard to provide the desk with some cute fall ideas for the family, Coco seemed to have other plans.
“She’s my little buddy tonight because someone just wasn’t getting along with the sitter,” the mom explains during the Oct. 10 episode.
Coco adds with a sinister look in her eyes that she “broke another one.”
In the sketch, the frazzled mom attempts to share some sweet activities like pressing a leaf into a book — one of her “favorites.”
“Mommy picks a book, and Coco goes and fetches a beautiful orange and red leaf from the yard,” the mom says.
Coco, however, shares how the activity really went down.
“I fell into a pile of leaves, and no one knew where I was for a day,” Coco says.

While the pair bicker, things really unravel when Coco claims she was missing for so long, she didn’t have dinner. According to Coco, the pizza her mom says she ate doesn’t count because she “didn’t like it.”
And mom just loses it.
“It doesn’t matter if you don’t like it,” the mom says, shrieking. “It’s still dinner if you ate it. You ate it all, and that’s dinner because you ate it.”
The mom attempts to share another lovely activity — making dried apple dolls.
“And fun fact: We got the apples just this weekend at a beautiful local apple orchard,” the mom says.
Coco, of course, has something to add.
“My mom stuck me in the corn maze for three hours so she could kiss a farmer,” she says.
Let’s just hope that the mom finally finds a worthy babysitter for Coco. She deserves a break.

title: Ben Affleck Reveals Hilarious Reason Why Matt Damon Passed Up Lead Role in ‘Animals’
summary: Ben Affleck reveals why his best friend, Matt Damon, couldn’t take on the leading role in his new Netflix thriller “Animals” as he had once hoped.
story: Ben Affleck reveals why his best friend, Matt Damon, couldn’t take on the leading role in his new Netflix thriller “Animals” as he had once hoped.

Affleck, who directed and starred in the new movie joined the Oct. 11 episode of Sunday Sitdown to chat about the film. And he revealed that Damon, initially his top pick to star in flick, had some other plans instead.
“I’m sure you’re aware, Ben, you were not the director’s first choice to star in this movie,” host Willie Geist joked.
Affleck confirmed the detail, explaining that Damon got another professional opportunity.

“Matt then ended up getting offered this little, kinda s----- little movie, ‘The Odyssey’ that bombed. And he was very embarrassed by it, of course.” Affleck said, laughing. “It just didn’t work at the box office, or with the critics, which happens sometimes.”
The “Animals” star went on to praise his friend, he played titular character Odysseus.
“He was really as happy as I’ve ever seen him the day that he got that job,” Affleck told Willie of Damon.
Damon and Affleck have been well-known besties, going through their first massive Hollywood moment together as they won the best screenplay Oscar in 1998 for “Good Will Hunting.”
“The whole idea of even being there was absurd,” Affleck recalled to Willie of attending the Oscars. “The year before, we’d watched the show from an apartment in Somerville, Massachusetts.”
The two have since acted in multiple films together including “The Last Duel” in 2021 and “Air” in 2023.

Additionally, Affleck has launched multiple production companies with Damon including Artists Equity, founded in November 2022. The company is behind a number of titles including “Air” and new film “Animals.”

The crime thriller, released Oct. 9, follows a high-profile Los Angeles mayoral candidate whose son is kidnapped, forcing the hopeful and his wife, played by Kerry Washington, into coming up with the $7 million ransom amid a financially stressful time in his campaign.
“I make movies mindful of the audience. But also, I did some things I really wanted to do in this that I think were really interesting,” the actor and director said of the new film.
Affleck beamed over his newest project, “I love this movie, ‘Animals.’ I really want people to see it.”

title: Mike Ditka’s Perfectly Unhinged Version of ‘Take Me Out To The Ballgame’ Resurfaces After Death
summary: A resurfaced video of Chicago Bears icon Mike Ditka singing during the seventh inning stretch at a baseball game is giving many fans something to smile about as they grieve the football giant’s death.
story: A resurfaced video of Chicago Bears icon Mike Ditka singing during the seventh inning stretch at a baseball game is giving many fans something to smile about as they grieve the football giant’s death.
The video features Ditka singing the classic “Take Me Out To The Ballgame” during a July 1998 match at Chicago’s Wrigley Field. And he definitely puts his own twist on the song.

In the clip, shared by MLB, Ditka raucously belts out the words, losing his voice several times throughout the song. Adding to his undeniable aura, Ditka also speeds up, leading the organist to attempt to match his pace.
It’s controlled chaos — just like the beloved football icon himself.
Ditka’s family announced his death Oct. 9. He was 86.

The Bears icon, who led the team to its only Super Bowl victory in  1986, was known for his big personality as much as he was for his gridiron prowess. And that charisma certainly shined during that 1998 Chicago Cubs game against the Pittsburgh Pirates.

That wasn’t even Ditka’s only famous rendition of the ballpark song. During a 2005 game at Wrigley Field between the Cubs and the Philadelphia Phillies, Ditka was joined by comedian Will Ferrell to lead the stadium in the song. The pair, who starred in comedy “Kicking & Screaming,” don’t exactly sing in-sync.

Ditka, who was inducted into the pro football Hall of Fame in 1988, has long been a source of comedy fodder. He even became the focus of a recurring sketch on “Saturday Night Live” in which a group of superfans, who look just like Ditka himself, hail the legendary coach as something of a god.

title: Alexander Skarsgard’s See-Through Dress Shoes Are Causing Chaos Across The Internet
summary: Actor Alexander Skarsgard showed up in a pair of see-through shoes to the annual BFI London Film Festival for an Oct. 8 screening of his upcoming romantic fantasy movie “Wicker.”
story: To call this a bold fashion choice would be an understatement.

Actor Alexander Skarsgard showed up to the annual BFI London Film Festival for an Oct. 8 screening of his upcoming romantic fantasy movie “Wicker.” But his look quickly became a focus of the event as he rocked a pair of see-through oxford shoes on the red carpet.
The shoes unsurprisingly elicited a range of responses from disgust to extreme lust.
Skarsgard’s transparent black shoes, which featured vinyl laces, were paired with a gold, metallic suit.
The oxfords, from fashion house Saint Laurent’s spring 2027 collection, made waves earlier this year when they debuted on the runway at  men’s Paris fashion week in June.

Corrado De Biase, the brand’s freelance design director of shoes, explained that the look is called “O. Fan,” after adult online platform OnlyFans. The shoes, he told Women’s Wear Daily, are a celebration of sexuality in the gay community.

“Because Monsieur Saint Laurent himself was really linked to those young community people when he was young,” De Biase told the outlet. “So it’s normal that a brand like us looks at that kind of thing. It’s been part of the house from the beginning.”
Saint Laurent creative director Anthony Vaccarello had a snarkier explanation for the footwear.
“I asked myself: ‘Why torture women with plastic shoes, but not men?’” Vaccarello said, according to WWD.
People across the internet had their own interpretations of the look. Some couldn’t help but wonder how Skarsgard was faring in the no-doubt sweaty shoes.
Others were just thirsting over the fashion choice.
“Oo our steak is too juicy, our lobster is too buttery, Alexander Skarsgaard is showing too much foot,” one commenter wrote on Instagram.

Well, 2026 appears to be the year of the gutsy red carpet footwear. Margaret Qualley sported a pair of Chanel’s “shoeless shoes” to the world premiere of “The Dog Stars” in August. The shoes were essentially black heels that were strapped to Qualley’s feet with two sets of laces and no soles.
While some deemed the shoes as chic, others joked that the barely-there footwear was a sign of “shrinkflation.”

title: Ben Affleck Admits He Trash Talks Kids Online While Playing ‘Fortnite’
summary: Ben Affleck recently revealed on the “New Heights” podcast that he sometimes gets into squabbles with kids on the internet while playing popular multiplayer open-world survival game “Fortnight.”
story: Gamer rage gets to everyone — even celebs.
Ben Affleck recently revealed on the “New Heights” podcast that he sometimes trash talks kids on the internet while playing popular multiplayer open-world survival game “Fortnight.”
Affleck, it appears, has a tough time taking the heat.

“Twelve-year-olds just f--- you up,” Affleck lamented to hosts Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce on the Oct. 7 podcast episode. “I get killed right away and they taunt you and s--- like ‘You suck! F--- you!’”
Affleck acknowledged that he ends up “getting in arguments” with the kids in the game’s chat.
“F--- you! I don’t suck,” he says in response to the taunting, Affleck told the podcast hosts. “I’m a grown man.”

Affleck, who’s currently promoting crime-thriller film “Animals,” joined the podcast to discuss the project. He explained that the costumes in the film are inspired by some of the outfits, referred to as skins, in “Fortnite.” The video game famously features different skins that can be upgraded through milestones, challenges and more.
As Affleck points out in the podcast, the game has also dropped exclusive and limited edition skins that have become some of the most coveted aspects of the game.
“My son and he’s like ‘For Christmas, can you get me these real skins for Fortnite?’ But they’re 300 bucks,” Affleck tells the podcast of the virtual costumes.
Affleck has long been an avid gamer. On the podcast, he explained that in addition to first-person shooter games, he’s a fan of sports games like football game “Madden” and basketball game “NBA 2K.”

The actor has also been open about his love for “Valorant,” a first-person tactical hero shooter video game. He’s been spotted at major tournaments and even joined a watch party livestream last year with esports team Sentinels.

title: ‘Pretty Little Liars’ Actor Says He Was Held At Gunpoint and Knifepoint in Mugging Attack
summary: Actor Keegan Allen, best known for his role in teen drama series “Pretty Little Liars,” alleges in an Oct. 9 video that he was violently mugged in West Hollywood by two masked men.
story: Actor Keegan Allen, best known for his role in teen drama series “Pretty Little Liars,” alleges in an Oct. 9 video that he was violently mugged in West Hollywood by two masked men.

In the video that was posted to his Instagram account, Allen, who appears to be bleeding from his head, says that he was robbed outside of Laurel Supply, an upscale grocery store in the Los Angeles neighborhood.

“These two dudes hit me in the head and pointed a gun at me with a knife, and then took off,” a visibly bloody Allen, catching his breath, says in the graphic video. He adds that the attackers took his watch.
Responding to comments under his video, the 37-year-old told fans that he went to the hospital following the incident and was “def concussed.”

The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department shared a statement in response to an NBC News request for comment on the incident. The department said that the LAPD’s Major Crimes Bureau is investigating the reported Oct. 8 armed robbery.
In the Instagram video, Allen shared footage of the alleged attack, which shows two men pointing a gun at a victim. One of the men bashes the victim over the head.
“Robbed at gunpoint and knifepoint by two young men that threatened to KILL me over my watch and would have! God said no tonight. My life for a watch,” he wrote in the caption of his post.
Allen wrote in response to a comment that one of the attackers also demanded a bracelet the actor was wearing, which led to the beating.
“I was trying to tell him it’s not easy to take off and said ‘you can take it off’ and he pistol whipped me,” Allen wrote.

The sheriff’s department said in the statement that deputies responded to the incident around 9:05 p.m. and spoke to a victim who reported being approached by two male suspects in black clothing. The victim told deputies that one suspect pointed a handgun at him while the other brandished a knife.
Actor Keegan Allen describes violent mugging incident

“During the incident, one of the suspects struck the victim in the face with the handgun, causing a laceration to his forehead,” the statement said. “The suspects took the victim’s watch and fled the location in an unknown vehicle.”
Personnel from the Los Angeles County Fire Department responded to the scene and medically evaluated the victim, who was not transported to the hospital, the statement said.
In his post, Allen called out Los Angeles mayor Karen Bass and California governor Gavin Newsom.
“Let’s hope all these flock cameras that @karenbassla @gavinnewsom and everyone thinks will stop crime can find these very dangerous criminals,” Allen wrote on Instagram.

In a statement sent to NBC News, Bass called the incident “egregious.” She also pointed out that West Hollywood is an independent city and that the LA County Sheriff’s Department is leading the investigation. It is technically not part of the city of Los Angeles.
“No one should have to experience something like this,” Bass said.

According to the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department, serious crimes in the area have decreased nearly 10% from January through August. Additionally, robberies have been on the decline. Statistics show that through August, there were 49 reported robberies. That’s a 21% decrease from the 62 incidents during the same period in 2025.
In response to recent October incidents, a department spokesperson said that the agency is increasing the number of deputies conducting patrols throughout the city.
“While these declines are encouraging, they do not diminish the seriousness of recent robberies or the fear felt by our community,” a spokesperson for the department said.

title: There’s a New Britney Spears Song. Listen to ‘She’ll Never Be Me’
summary: Britney Spears fans got an unexpected surprise in the form of a previously unreleased song from the pop icon.
story: Britney Spears fans got an unexpected surprise in the form of a previously unreleased song from the pop icon.
On Oct. 9, Spears and her team dropped the song “She’ll Never Be Me,” which was recorded for her 2001 self-titled third album “Britney.”
The song comes weeks before the album celebrates its 25th anniversary with a special edition re-release, “Britney (25th Anniversary Edition),” that includes songs from the vault.
“She’ll Never Be Me” is a quintessential Britney Spears track with its bubblegum pop, early aughts sound, girl power lyrics and the singer’s signature girlish and gritty vocals.
The 3-minute track talks about a former lover who is now with someone that looks just like her.

“You know I’m one of a kind/Boy, what’s this I see/Your girl, she looks just like me/Blond hair and dressed to a T,” she begins. “You tell me how can this be/Does she know I was the one/Who used to turn you on/But you don’t want to talk about it.”
According to the song’s YouTube description, Spears is credited as the lyricist, associated performer and composer.
Her ex Justin Timberlake is also featured as a lyricist and composer, along with Bradley Daymond and Alex Greggs. Riprock ‘n’ Alex G is a producer.

“She’ll Never Be Me” is one of five new songs included in the “Britney” re-release, including “Am I a Sinner,” “When I Say So,” “My Big Secret” and “Right Now (Taste The Victory)” from her 2002 Pepsi commercial.
Fans will get to hear the songs when “Britney (25th Anniversary Edition)” is released on Nov. 6.
The last time Spears shared a new song was 2023’s “Mind Your Business” with Will.i.am. In 2020, she also dropped a never-before-heard collaboration with the Backstreet Boys titled “Matches.”
The song was featured in a deluxe edition of her 2016 album “Glory.”

title: Crystal Harris Posts Message She Sent Jessica Biel With Plea to ‘Reconsider’ Playing Hugh Hefner’s Wife in Movie
summary: Hugh Hefner’s widow, Crystal Harris, is asking Jessica Biel not to portray a fictional version of the Playboy founder’s wife in the upcoming movie “Playmates.”
story: Hugh Hefner’s widow, Crystal Harris, is asking Jessica Biel not to portray a fictional version of the Playboy founder’s wife in the upcoming movie “Playmates.”

Harris, who was married to Hefner from 2012 until his death in 2017, posted a screenshot of a text on Instagram on Oct. 8 that she sent Biel, urging her to pass up the role of Hefner’s fictional wife.
“Please reconsider playing Hugh Hefner’s ‘wife’ if this film intends to romanticize him or the Playboy world,” Harris wrote in a message to Biel, according to the screenshot she shared on Instagram.

“I was actually his wife, and I experienced sexual, emotional, financial and physical abuse in that relationship. Many other women have come forward with allegations of rape, coercion, drugging and exploitation as well.

“There are also deeply troubling concerns involving minors. I hope everyone involved in this film takes the time to listen to the women who lived it before helping Hollywood turn it back into nostalgia.”
TODAY.com has reached out to Biel for comment about Harris’ post, as well as Harris for any further comment about what she wrote. Neither responded.
TODAY.com also reached out toHefner’s estate for comment about Harris’ allegations of experiencing “rape, coercion, drugging and exploitation,” but did not hear back.
The film is being made by Searchlight Pictures, which not did reply to TODAY.com’s request for comment about Harris’ post or Biel’s casting in the movie.

Variety reported Oct. 6 that Biel has joined the cast of “Playmates,” a coming-of-age story about a 13-year-old girl who befriends a woman competing with other hopefuls to become Playmate of the Month. Bill Pullman, Lily-Rose Depp and Indiana Elle are also attached to star in it.
Biel is slated to play Hefner’s wife in the movie. According to Variety, the character is fictional and not based on a real person.
Hefner was married two other times, to Kimberley Conrad from 1989 to 2010 and Millie Williams from 1949 to 1959.
Harris followed up her post with another one, in which she showed appreciation for the “overwhelming response” she received.
“So many women are speaking up, sharing their experiences, and expressing that they’ve simply had enough,” she wrote.

“Victim blaming is still far too common, especially when it comes to narcissistic and emotional abuse. I know that not everyone has experienced these dynamics firsthand, and I’m genuinely glad for those who haven’t. But I also hope we can listen to and support the women who have, even when their experiences are difficult to understand.”

Harris also said she wants “to support women” and express her hope that the movie is “not something that will glorify Hugh Hefner. With women in the leading roles, my hope is that the film ultimately delivers a message of empowerment: that women can find fulfillment, independence, and a sense of self beyond Playboy.”
In 2024, Harris penned a memoir, “Only Say Good Things: Surviving ‘Playboy’ and Finding Myself,” in which she wrote that living in the famed Playboy Mansion was like living in a prison.

“I always had to be home by six o’clock. If I wasn’t, it was a problem. He would be upset. He would be yelling my name through the house,” she says of Hugh Hefner, writing that she felt like Rapunzel locked in a tower.
“I didn’t know then that I could rescue myself. I didn’t always know I needed to be rescued, but I knew I was trapped,” she added.
Harris also said Hefner was a “narcissist” and had a need to control the women who lived in the mansion.
“It’s like he wanted us to beg him for something, so he could feel even more powerful and probably have us feel small,” she told TODAY.com in 2024.
“It was weird and it was hard. Looking back, he did use me and manipulate me for his own gain in every way,” she continued.
In August, Harris said Hefner was “very abusive” and that she was “brainwashed” when she appeared on the “No One Asked Her” podcast.

“So I just thought I was the crazy one because all of the media put Hef on such a pedestal that I’m like, ‘OK, if they all see him as this larger-than-life amazing human, there must be something wrong with me,” she said.
Hefner has been accused of sexual misconduct before, with multiple allegations leveled against him in the 2022 A&E series “Secrets of Playboy,” released five years after he died in 2017.

“This series contains allegations of wrongdoing over decades by Hugh Hefner and others associated with him,” read a statement at the end of each episode. “The vast majority of allegations have not been the subject of criminal investigations or charges, and they do not constitute proof of guilt.”

title: How Realistic Is ‘War’? A Divorce Lawyer Says this 1 Move Would Get Characters Disbarred
summary: A UK divorce lawyer reacts to the HBO drama “War” including the mole and serving papers on the red carpet.
story: “Take It From Me” is a TODAY.com series where experts use their wisdom to explain trends or make recommendations within their fields. In this story, a U.K. divorce lawyer weighs in on “War.”

HBO’s new legal drama “War” gives viewers an unflinching look behind the scenes of a nasty, high-powered divorce. The series focuses on the lengths divorce lawyers from rival law firms in London will go to score a profitable win for their clients.

The depiction of ruthless attorneys scheming to gain the upper hand in a pending divorce “heavily dramatized for viewing public consumption,” and not necessarily realistic, said Daniel Sugaré, the head of family law department at Sugaré & Co. Solicitors in the U.K.

Set in London, “War” tells the story of the shattering end of the decade-long marriage between tech billionaire Morgan Henderson (Dominic West) and his Hollywood star wife, Carla Duval (Sienna Miller), resulting in divorce.
Morgan and Carla hire lawyers from rival London law firms, Cathcarts & Sons and Taylor & Byrne, respectively, to take each other down in court.
Here’s what a real divorce lawyer thinks of the show’s pilot.
Hiring a Lawyer As a Mole? That’s a Big No-No
One of lawyers’ most egregious antics would cause them to lose their law licenses in real life, Sugaré said.
Specifically, Cathcarts & Sons’s move to send struggling young lawyer Johnny Warren (Archie Renaux) to Taylor & Byrne to act as a mole for their case.
“(Johnny) would be struck off immediately by the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA),” Sugaré said of the mole.
“You’ve got a duty to your clients to act confidentially, act in their best interests, and by sharing information like in that manner, that they would be bound for disciplinary procedures,” he added.
The higher-ups at Cathcarts & Sons who orchestrated the scheme “would also face significant legal consequences from the SRA and potentially criminal proceedings,” he said.
The bad behavior of the lawyers on the show veers far from what real-life attorneys aim to do: help clients remain calm and focused so they can come to an agreement.
“In certain cases, you have to act in an aggressive way to protect your client’s interest,” said Sugaré. “But in the show, it seems like they’re doing that more than what is necessary.”
Carla’s Cheating Scheme

The show starts with Morgan sleeping with a young woman named Flora (Rose Williams). Turns out the moment has been orchestrated by Carla. She wants to prove that Morgan is unfaithful, and in doing so, exploit the prenuptial’s infidelity clause.
But will Carla’s scheme actually work? Not so fast, Sugaré said.
“An affair is not ordinarily a legal escape route from a prenuptial agreement,” Sugaré said.
Sugaré said infidelity clauses are “unusual” in England, as prenups generally deal with financial agreements rather than penalties for cheating.

“Even if this agreement contains an infidelity clause, Carla could not assume that the court would enforce it. While these cases are fact specific, proof of an affair would not ordinarily invalidate the agreement or entitle her to a larger settlement,” he said.
Serving Papers on the Red Carpet
Morgan and Carla race to be the one to serve the other with divorce papers. Morgan ultimately Carla divorce papers on a red carpet.
It’s a biting and humiliating moment, but not necessarily a tactic that gives Morgan an edge, according to Sugaré.
“The race to start divorce proceedings makes good television, but being the applicant does not give Morgan priority over the assets or make the judge more sympathetic to him,” Sugaré said.
And while serving a divorce application on a red carpet is “legally permissible,” it’s normally facilitated via email, Sugaré says.
So, Is Divorce Really ‘War’?
As for the show’s title? Sugaré said war is an apt metaphor for the potential brutality of divorce.
“It can get aggressive. It can be vicious. It can be personal, and the job of the lawyer is to try and rein your client in,” Sugaré said.

He explained a good lawyer tries to help clients stop ruminating about their emotions and the end of the marriage and instead prepare to “reach sensible agreements or make big decisions about (their) future,” he said.
His advice for anyone entering into a marriage? At the risk of sounding like an “anti-love guy,” Sugaré suggests both parties sign a prenuptial agreement.

“In the right circumstances, a prenuptial agreement can give both parties clarity and certainty. It may not be the most romantic conversation before a wedding, but being open about finances at the outset can prevent far greater conflict later.”

title: 4 Biggest Takeaways From Michael Douglas’ Explosive Memoir
summary: Actor Michael Douglas, who cemented his legendary status after a decadeslong career in Hollywood,” reflects on his wildly eventful life in new memoir “One Helluva Ride.”
story: Actor Michael Douglas, who cemented his legendary status after a decadeslong career in Hollywood,” reflects on his wildly eventful life in new memoir “One Helluva Ride.” And that includes some pretty explosive confessions.

Douglas, best known for his roles in blockbuster films “Wall Street” and “Basic Instinct,” details his personal sagas involving everything from infidelity to struggles with parenting in what many readers have already considered a bombshell of a book.

Now 82, the actor writes that he is refusing to shy away from any aspect of his life, and that includes some of the more unsavory elements, acknowledging that he spent a large part of his career portraying the “modern, flawed, American male.” And that archetype, he adds, “wasn’t exactly a stretch for me.”

With eight decades of drama — literally and figuratively — to unpack, Douglas says in the sprawling, 500-page memoir released Oct. 6, that the account reveals “who I became and the choices I made along the way.”
“I’ve lived a large part of my life in the public eye, but I’m a very private person,” Douglas writes. “Fame can blur the truth. Now it’s time to finally bring it all back into focus.”
Here are some of the most eye-opening highlights from “One Helluva Ride.”
He Had a Complicated Relationship With His Father, Screen Legend Kirk Douglas
Michael Douglas had a complicated, sometimes tenuous relationship with his father Kirk Douglas. And it was one that ended up shaping much of his professional and personal life, he wrote.

Kirk Douglas, who was born Issur Danielovitch Demsky, was the child of Russian Jewish immigrants and had spent much of his upbringing enduring poverty and domestic violence, the memoir says. Aspects of his difficult beginnings bled into the way in which Kirk Douglas parented — a role that, the younger Douglas wrote, involved violence and rage that at times were rationalized as “care.”

But against a backdrop of family tensions were also professional pressures, Michael Douglas wrote. In the book he recounted the way in which he’d struggled to make a name for himself, independent of his father, often having to contend with inevitable comparisons between the two. It was difficult, Michael Douglas wrote, as someone whose Hollywood dad had become synonymous with an iconic gladiator hero.
“I should have been born Mikhail Danielovitch, grandson of a ragman,” he wrote in the memoir. “Instead, I was born Michael Kirk Douglas, son of Spartacus.”

They also experienced some frictions in the field, made all the more complicated by their family dynamic.
